Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 1:

Surat an-Nisa' [Madaniyya, and its verses are 176 or 177; it was revealed after al-Mumtahana]

﴿O mankind﴾, i.e., the people of Makkah, ﴿fear your Lord﴾, i.e., His punishment, by obeying Him, ﴿who created you from one soul﴾, Adam, ﴿and created from it its mate﴾, Hawwa' (Eve), with the long vowel (madd), from a rib of his left ribs, ﴿and spread﴾, scattered and dispersed, ﴿from the two of them﴾, from Adam and Hawwa', ﴿men in great number and women﴾ in great number. ﴿And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another﴾: in it the ta' in the original is assimilated into the sin (idgham), and in another reading it is recited with lightening by deleting it, i.e., tatasa'alun, ﴿by Him﴾, among yourselves, where one of you says to another, "I ask you by Allah, and I adjure you by Allah." ﴿And [fear] the wombs﴾, that you sever them; and in another reading it is recited with the genitive (jarr), as a conjunction upon the pronoun in bihi (by Him), and they used to adjure one another by the womb. ﴿Indeed Allah has ever been over you a watchful observer﴾, guarding your deeds so that He will recompense you for them, i.e., He has never ceased being characterized by that.

It was revealed concerning an orphan who asked his guardian for his property, and the guardian refused him. ﴿And give the orphans their property﴾, the young ones who have no father, ﴿when they reach maturity﴾. ﴿And do not substitute the bad﴾, the unlawful, ﴿for the good﴾, the lawful, meaning, do not take the good [from their property] in exchange for it, as you do when you take the good from the property of the orphan and put the bad from your own property in its place. ﴿And do not consume their property along with your own property﴾, combined with it. ﴿Indeed, that is a great sin﴾, a transgression, ﴿great﴾, immense. When this was revealed, they became reluctant to take charge of orphans, and among them were those who had under them ten or eight wives, and would not treat them equitably, so this was revealed.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 3:

﴿And if you fear﴾ that you will not ﴿act justly﴾, i.e., be equitable, ﴿towards the orphans﴾, and so you feel uneasy about their affairs, then fear likewise that you will not be equitable among the women when you marry them. ﴿Then marry﴾, i.e., take in marriage, ﴿whatever﴾ (ma, here with the meaning of man, "whoever") ﴿seems good to you of women, two, three, or four﴾, i.e., two, three, or four, and do not exceed that number. ﴿But if you fear﴾ that you will not ﴿be equitable﴾ toward them in maintenance and in the division of nights, ﴿then one﴾, marry only her, ﴿or﴾ limit yourselves to ﴿what your right hands possess﴾ of female slaves, since they do not have the rights that wives have. ﴿That﴾, i.e., marrying up to four only, or one, or taking concubines, ﴿is nearer﴾, closer, ﴿to your not being unjust﴾, i.e., not oppressing.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 4:

﴿And give﴾ [i.e., bestow] ﴿to the women their dowries﴾ — the plural of ṣadaqa, meaning their bridal gifts (muhūr), ﴿as a gift﴾ — a verbal noun of ʿaṭiyya, ﴿graciously﴾ [lit. from good self/willingness of heart]. ﴿But if they give you willingly of it, any part of it﴾ — a tamyīz (specification) transferred from the subject; i.e., their selves are pleased to give you some part of the ṣadāq, and so they give it to you, ﴿then consume it with satisfaction and pleasure﴾ [hanīʾan] — pleasant, ﴿and wholesome﴾ [marīʾan] — with good outcome, with no harm to you in the Hereafter. It was revealed in refutation of those who disliked this.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 5:

﴿And do not give﴾ O guardians ﴿the foolish﴾ (al-sufaha'), those who squander wealth, from among the men, the women and the children, ﴿your property﴾, i.e., the property that is in your hands, ﴿which Allah has made for you a means of support﴾ (qiyaman). It is a verbal noun from qama, meaning that by it your livelihood stands and the welfare of your children is maintained. So they would place it in other than its proper place. In another reading it is qiyaman, plural of qima (value), that by which goods are valued. ﴿And provide for them from it﴾, i.e., feed them from it, ﴿and clothe them, and speak to them a known word﴾, i.e., promise them a good promise by giving them their property when they become mature.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 6:

﴿And test the orphans﴾ (ibtalu): test them (ikhtabiru), [the orphans] before puberty, in their religion and in their management of their affairs ﴿until, when they reach marriageable age﴾ (al-nikah), i.e., they become fit for it by wet dreams (al-ihtilam) or by age, and that is completing fifteen years according to al-Shafi'i ﴿then if you perceive﴾ (anastum), i.e., you see ﴿in them sound judgment﴾ (rushdan), i.e., righteousness in their religion and their property, ﴿then hand over to them their property, and do not consume it﴾ (ta'kulu-ha), O guardians, ﴿wastefully﴾ (israfan), i.e., without right, ﴿and hastily﴾ (wa-bidaran), i.e., hurrying to spend it, ﴿lest they grow up﴾ (an yakbaru), [becoming] of sound judgment, for then it would be incumbent upon you to hand it over to them. ﴿And whoever is wealthy﴾ among the guardians ﴿let him abstain﴾ (fal-yasta'fif), i.e., let him refrain from the property of the orphan and withhold from consuming it. ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat﴾ of it ﴿in a reasonable manner﴾ (bil-ma'ruf), i.e., in proportion to the wage of his work. ﴿Then when you hand over to them﴾, i.e., to the orphans, ﴿their property, have witnesses against them﴾ that they have received it and that you are discharged, lest a dispute arise and you have to return to evidence. This is a command of guidance. ﴿And sufficient is Allah﴾ (the ba' is superfluous) ﴿as Reckoner﴾ (hasiban), a Guardian over the deeds of His creatures and their Reckoner.

It was revealed as a refutation of what was practiced in the pre-Islamic period (jahiliyyah), namely the denial of inheritance to women and children: ﴿For men there is a share﴾ — the sons and the relatives — ﴿of what the parents and the close relatives leave behind﴾ — the deceased — ﴿and for women there is a share of what the parents and the close relatives leave behind, whether it is little or much﴾ — i.e., of the property — ﴿a share ordained﴾ — decreed, fixed, to be handed over to them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 8:

﴿And when the division [of the inheritance] is attended﴾ by ﴿the relatives﴾ [of the deceased], i.e., the kindred who do not inherit, ﴿and the orphans and the needy, then provide for them from it﴾, i.e., give them something before the division, ﴿and speak to them﴾, O guardians, ﴿a kind word﴾, i.e., a good one, ﴿if the heirs are minors﴾, by apologising to them that you do not own it and that it belongs to the minors. It has been said that this [verse] is abrogated (mansukh). It has also been said that it is not, but people have been negligent in leaving it. On this view it is recommended (nadb). From Ibn ʿAbbas [it is reported that] it is obligatory (wajib).

Let them fear (ﷲ) — that is, let them be fearful for the orphans ﴿who, if they were to leave behind them weak offspring﴾ — that is, were about to leave behind them after their death ﴿weak offspring﴾, young children — ﴿they would fear for them﴾, [fear] of their being lost. ﴿So let them be mindful of Allah﴾ regarding the matter of the orphans, and let them treat them as they would want their own offspring after them to be treated. ﴿And let them speak﴾ to the one whose death is approaching ﴿a fitting word﴾, a right word: by urging him to give in charity no more than a third of his wealth and leave the rest to his heirs, and not leave them destitute.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 10:

﴿Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly﴾ without right, ﴿they are only consuming fire into their bellies﴾, meaning, filling them with it, ﴿Fire﴾ because it leads to it. ﴿And they will burn﴾ (with the verb in the active and passive voice: "they will enter") ﴿in a blaze﴾, a fierce fire in which they will be burned.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 11:

﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children﴾ He commands you regarding (shaʾn) your children, with what follows: ﴿for the male, a share equal to that of two females﴾ of them, ﴿equal to the portion (ḥaẓẓ) of two females﴾ if they are together with him. Then he has half the property and they (the two) have the half. If there is with him one female, then she has a third and he has two-thirds. If he is alone, he takes the whole property. ﴿But if they are women﴾ i.e., the children, ﴿only, more than two﴾ then ﴿for them is two-thirds of what he left﴾ (the deceased). Likewise two women, because it is for the two sisters by His saying: ﴿for them two-thirds of what he left﴾; so they (two daughters) have more right to it. And because a daughter deserves a third along with a son, so along with a female she has more right (to two-thirds). ("More than two," fawq) has been said to be a connective particle (ṣila), and it has been said it is to ward off the suspicion that the share increases with the increase in number, since it has been understood that two daughters deserve two-thirds from the placing of a third for one female along with a male. ﴿And if she is one﴾ (the daughter), ﴿she has the half﴾ — and in one reading, with the nominative (wāḥidatun), so kāna is complete. ﴿And for his parents, to each one of them the sixth of what he left, if he has a child﴾, male or female. The point of the substitution (badal) is to convey that the two do not share in it. The grandson (ibn al-ibn) is joined with the child, and the grandfather (al-jadd) with the father. ﴿But if he has no child and his two parents inherit him﴾, only them, or together with a spouse, ﴿then for his mother is the third﴾ — the hamza of ʾummih is read with a ḍamma and with a kasra, to avoid moving from a ḍamma to a kasra, since it is heavy in both positions — ﴿the third﴾, i.e., a third of the property, or what remains after the spouse, and the rest is for the father. ﴿But if he has siblings﴾, i.e., two or more, male or female, ﴿then for his mother is the sixth﴾, and the rest is for the father, and the siblings get nothing. The inheritance of those mentioned is as mentioned ﴿after﴾ the execution of ﴿a bequest he bequeaths﴾ — the verb is built for the active and the passive — ﴿or﴾ the payment of ﴿a debt﴾ upon him. The mention of the bequest before the debt, although the debt is prior in discharge, is for the importance attached to it. ﴿Your fathers and your sons﴾ are the subject (mubtadaʾ), whose predicate is: ﴿you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit﴾. ﴿You do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit﴾ in this world and the Hereafter. So one may think that his son is more beneficial to him, so he gives him the inheritance, and then the father would be more beneficial, and vice versa. Only Allah knows this, so He has prescribed for you the inheritance, ﴿as an obligation from Allah; indeed Allah is ever Knowing﴾ of His creation, ﴿Wise﴾ in what He has ordained for them, i.e., He has never ceased to be characterized by that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 12:

﴿And for you is half of what your wives leave, if they have no child﴾ (whether from you or from another), ﴿but if they have a child, then for you is a quarter of what they leave, after any bequest they make or debt﴾. The grandson through a son is added to the child in this ruling by consensus (ijma') (the consensus of the scholars). ﴿And for them (i.e., the wives, who are plural at first)﴾ ﴿is a quarter of what you leave, if you have no child; but if you have a child﴾ (from them or from others), ﴿then for them is an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you make or debt﴾. The son's child in this matter is like the child, by consensus. ﴿And if a man whose estate is inherited (yuwrath) is one who has neither father nor child (kalala)﴾ — here "kalala" is a description, and the predicate is — ﴿or a woman (whose estate is inherited by kalala)﴾, ﴿and he (i.e., the deceased, the kalala) has a brother or a sister﴾, i.e., from the mother. Ibn Mas'ud and others recited it this way. ﴿Then each one of them receives a sixth﴾ of what he left. ﴿But if they are more than that﴾, i.e., more than one, ﴿then they share in the third﴾, the male and female among them being equal in this. ﴿After any bequest that is made or debt, without harm﴾ — this is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in "yuusa" (is made), i.e., not causing harm to the heirs by bequeathing more than a third. ﴿A bequest﴾ is an emphatic verbal noun (masdar) for "yusikum" (He instructs you). ﴿From Allah. And Allah is All-Knowing﴾ of what He has ordained for His creation of the obligatory shares, ﴿All-Forbearing﴾ in delaying punishment for those who oppose Him. The Sunnah has specified the inheritance of those mentioned to be restricted to those who have no impediment, such as killing, difference of religion, or slavery.

"That" — the rulings mentioned, from the matter of the orphans and what follows — "are the limits of Allah," His laws which He set down for His servants that they might act by them and not transgress them. "And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger" in what He has judged, "He will admit him" — with the yā' and the nūn (the shift in person, iltifāt).

Qur'anic quotations: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him﴾ with both readings (bi-l-wajhayn), ﴿to a Fire, to abide therein forever; and for him is a humiliating punishment﴾ therein, ﴿humiliating﴾ meaning one who causes humiliation. The pronouns in the two verses are treated according to the wording of "man" (raʿiya lafẓ man), while in "khalidin" (abiding) its meaning is observed (wa-fi khalidīna maʿnāhā).

And those of your women who commit lewdness (al-fahisha), [i.e., adultery (al-zina)], — call against them four witnesses from among you, i.e., from among your male Muslims. Then if they testify, confine them to houses (fi al-buyut) — i.e., imprison them and prevent them from mixing with people — until death takes them (yatawaffahunna al-mawt), i.e., His angels, or until God makes for them a way (sabilan), a path out of it. They were commanded with this at the beginning of Islam; then God made for them a way: for a virgin (al-bikr), a hundred lashes and exile for a year; and for a married woman (al-muhsana), stoning. And in the hadith, when he (ﷺ) explained the punishment, he said: "Take from me, take from me; God has made for them a way" — related by Muslim.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 16:

﴿And those two of you who commit it⟩ (the nūn is read with both light and heavy stress). ﴿Commit it﴾ means the immorality: fornication (zinā) or sodomy (liwāṭ). ﴿Of you﴾ means men. ﴿Harm them﴾ by verbal abuse and beating with sandals. ﴿But if they repent﴾ from it ﴿and amend﴾ their conduct, ﴿then leave them alone﴾ and do not harm them. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Accepting of repentance﴾ from whoever repents, ﴿Merciful﴾ to them.

This verse is abrogated (mansūkh) by the prescribed punishment (al-ḥadd) if it refers to fornication. Likewise, if it refers to sodomy, according to al-Shāfiʿī (the founder of the Shāfiʿī school of law), except that the one who is sodomized is not stoned according to him, even if he is married (muḥṣan); rather he is flogged and exiled. The meaning of sodomy is more apparent, by the evidence of the dual form of the pronoun. The first view is that it means the male and female adulterers. It is refuted by their being specified with "min" (of you), which is connected to the pronoun of the men, and by their sharing in the harm, the repentance and the turning away. And this is restricted to men, because of what was mentioned earlier regarding women in confinement.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 17:

﴿Repentance is only [accepted] from Allah﴾, i.e., the repentance which He has prescribed upon Himself to accept by His bounty, ﴿for those who do evil﴾, i.e., disobedience, ﴿in ignorance﴾ (a circumstantial clause, meaning: ignorant when they disobey their Lord), ﴿then repent soon﴾ (a period of time, meaning: before they reach the death throes), ﴿those Allah will forgive﴾, i.e., He will accept their repentance, ﴿and Allah is ever Knowing﴾ of His creation, ﴿Wise﴾ in His dealings with them.

Qur'an 4:18 (Tafsir al-Jalalayn)

﴿And repentance is not for those who commit misdeeds﴾, the sins, ﴿until, when death approaches one of them﴾ and he begins the death-rattle, ﴿he says﴾ at the moment of witnessing what he is in, ﴿"Indeed, I repent now"﴾; so that does not benefit him, nor is it accepted from him. ﴿Nor for those who die while they are disbelievers﴾; if they repent in the Hereafter at the sight of the punishment, it will not be accepted from them. ﴿For those We have prepared﴾, We have readied ﴿a painful punishment﴾, painful in its effect.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 19:

﴿O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by compulsion﴾ i.e., their persons. ﴿By compulsion﴾: with a fatḥa or a ḍamma on the first letter, both are dialectal variants; i.e., forcing them to that. In the pre-Islamic period (al-Jāhiliyyah), they would inherit the wives of their relatives. Then, if they wished, they would marry them without a dowry (ṣadāq), or they would give them in marriage and take their dowry, or they would restrain them (ʿaḍal) until they ransomed themselves with what they had inherited, or until they died, whereupon they would inherit them. So they were forbidden from this. ﴿Nor﴾ that ﴿you restrain them﴾ i.e., prevent your wives from marrying others by keeping them while you have no desire for them, out of harm ﴿so that you may take away part of what you have given them﴾ of the bridal gift (mahr), ﴿unless they commit a clear immorality﴾ with a fatḥa or kasra on the yā' (mubayyinah / mubayyinatin): i.e., they have made it clear, or it is clear, namely fornication or disobedience (nushūz). Then it is permissible for you to harm them until they ransom themselves from you and seek khul' (divorce by compensation). ﴿And live with them in kindness﴾ i.e., in general terms, in speech, maintenance and lodging. ﴿But if you dislike them﴾ then be patient. ﴿It may be that you dislike a thing and Allah makes in it much good﴾ perhaps He will place that good in them, by granting you from them a righteous child.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 20:

﴿And if you desire to replace a wife with another wife﴾ i.e., to take her in place of her, by divorcing her ﴿and﴾ you have ﴿given one of them﴾ i.e., of the wives ﴿a great amount﴾ of wealth, as dower ﴿then do not take anything from it. Would you take it by slander﴾ i.e., unjustly ﴿and a manifest sin﴾ clear. Both are in the accusative as circumstantial clauses (ḥāl), and the interrogation is for rebuke and denial in His saying:

"And how could you take it back when you have gone in to one another and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?" That is: in what manner? "When you have gone in to one another": reached one another, by intercourse which establishes the dower. "And they have taken from you a firm covenant": a strong, binding pledge, which is what Allah commanded: keeping them in kindness or releasing them with goodness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 22:

﴿And do not marry what your fathers married of women,﴾ with "what" meaning "those who" (man), ﴿except﴾ but ﴿what has already passed,﴾ of your action in that regard; for it is pardoned. ﴿Indeed, it﴾ that is, their marriage, ﴿was an abomination﴾ ugly, ﴿and hatred﴾ a cause of hatred from Allah, which is the strongest loathing, ﴿and evil was it as a way﴾ how bad a path that was.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 23:

﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers﴾ to marry them; this includes the grandmothers from the father's or the mother's side. ﴿and your daughters﴾; this includes the daughters of your children, however low they descend. ﴿and your sisters﴾ from the father's or the mother's side. ﴿and your paternal aunts﴾, that is, the sisters of your fathers and your grandfathers. ﴿and your maternal aunts﴾, that is, the sisters of your mothers and your grandmothers. ﴿and the daughters of your brother and the daughters of your sister﴾; their children are included among them. ﴿and your mothers who have nursed you﴾, before the completion of the two years, five feedings, as the hadith explains. ﴿and your milk-sisters﴾. By the Sunnah, the following are added to this: the daughters of these (milk-relations), and their mothers-in-law (the mothers of those whom they nursed, i.e. the wives of the one who sired the milk), and the paternal aunts, maternal aunts, daughters of the brother and daughters of the sister of these (milk-relations), based on the hadith: "What is forbidden by nursing is forbidden by lineage." Related by al-Bukhari and Muslim. ﴿and your wives' mothers and your stepdaughters﴾; "raba'ib" is the plural of "rabibah," who is the daughter of a wife from another husband. ﴿who are in your guardianship﴾; this is a descriptive qualifier that agrees with the usual case, so it carries no implied restriction. ﴿of your wives with whom you have consummated the marriage﴾, that is, had intercourse with them. ﴿But if you have not consummated the marriage with them, there is no blame upon you﴾ in marrying their daughters, if you have separated from them. ﴿and the wives of your sons who are from your loins﴾; this excludes those whom you have adopted, so it is permissible for you to marry their wives. ﴿and that you combine two sisters﴾ by lineage or nursing, through marriage. By the Sunnah, combining a woman with her paternal aunt or maternal aunt is added to this. It is permissible to marry each one of them individually, or to own both as slave-concubines, but one may have intercourse with only one of them. ﴿except﴾ but ﴿what has already occurred﴾ in the Jahiliyyah of marrying some of what has been mentioned; there is no blame upon you for it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ of what occurred from you before the prohibition, ﴿Merciful﴾ to you in that.

**﴿And﴾** ﴿forbidden to you are the married women﴾, meaning those who have husbands, ﴿among women﴾, to marry them before they are separated from their husbands, ﴿whether free or Muslim, or not﴾. ﴿Except what your right hands possess﴾ of slave women taken as captives, so you may have intercourse with them, even if they have husbands in the abode of war, after ascertaining that their wombs are empty (istibra'). ﴿The decree of God﴾ is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar), meaning: God has prescribed this ﴿for you﴾. ﴿And lawful﴾ (read in both the active and passive voice) ﴿for you is what lies beyond that﴾, meaning apart from those women who are forbidden to you, ﴿that you seek﴾, that is, desire women ﴿with your wealth﴾, as a dowry (sadaq) or a price, ﴿chaste, not fornicating﴾, that is, married, not committing unlawful sexual intercourse (zina). ﴿So for whatever﴾, that is, whoever, ﴿you have enjoyed﴾, that is, benefited, ﴿of them﴾, from those you have married, through intercourse, ﴿give them their due payment﴾, meaning their dowries which you have specified for them ﴿as an obligation. And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree upon﴾ between yourselves and them ﴿after the obligation﴾, whether by reducing it, reducing part of it, or increasing it. ﴿Indeed, God is ever Knowing﴾ of His creation, ﴿Wise﴾ in what He has ordained for them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 25:

﴿And whoever among you cannot afford﴾ (ṭawl), i.e., wealth, ﴿to marry free﴾ women ﴿believing women﴾, this being a case of following what is usual, so it has no implied restriction; ﴿then from what your right hands possess﴾ of ﴿your believing young women﴾ may [he] marry. ﴿And Allah is most knowing of your faith﴾, so rely on its outward appearance and leave the inner matters to Him, for He is the one who knows their excellence, and many a slave woman surpasses a free woman in it. This is an encouragement to marry slave women. ﴿You are of one another﴾, i.e., you and they are equal in religion, so do not disdain marrying them. ﴿So marry them with the permission of their families﴾, their masters, ﴿and give them their wages﴾, i.e., give them ﴿their dowries﴾ ﴿in a fair manner﴾, without delay or reduction, ﴿chaste﴾, modest (a circumstantial state), ﴿not unchaste﴾, those who fornicate openly, ﴿nor taking secret lovers﴾, paramours who commit fornication with them in secret. ﴿And when they are married﴾ (uḥṣinna, i.e., they are given in marriage; in another reading with the active voice, tazawwajna, "they marry"), ﴿and if they commit a lewd act﴾, fornication, ﴿then for them is half the punishment of free chaste women﴾, the virgins, if they fornicate, ﴿of the torment﴾, i.e., the prescribed penalty; so they are flogged fifty lashes and exiled for half a year. Slaves are assimilated to them by analogy. He did not make chastity (iḥṣān) a condition for the obligation of the penalty, to indicate that there is no stoning for them at all. ﴿That﴾, i.e., marrying slave women when one cannot afford free women, ﴿is for him who fears﴾, fears, ﴿sin﴾ (ʿanat), i.e., fornication; its root meaning is hardship, and fornication is so named because it causes hardship through the prescribed penalty in this world and the punishment in the Hereafter, ﴿among you﴾. This is unlike one who does not fear it among free men, for it is not lawful for him to marry them; likewise, one who is able to afford a free woman. This is the view of al-Shafiʿi. The qualifier ﴿from your believing young women﴾ excludes unbelieving ones: it is not lawful for him to marry them even if he lacks means and fears sin. ﴿And that you be patient﴾ concerning marrying slave women ﴿is better for you﴾, so that the child does not become a slave. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ in granting latitude in this matter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 26:

﴿Allah desires to make clear to you﴾ the laws of your religion and the interests of your affairs, ﴿and to guide you to the ways﴾ (sunan: paths, ways) ﴿of those before you﴾ from among the prophets, concerning what is lawful and unlawful, so that you may follow them, ﴿and to turn to you in forgiveness﴾ (yarji'u bikum: He returns you) from your disobedience in which you were, to His obedience, ﴿and Allah is Knowing﴾ of you, ﴿Wise﴾ in what He has ordained for you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 27:

﴿And Allah desires to accept your repentance﴾ He repeated it in order to build upon it ﴿but those who follow their desires desire that you should deviate with a great deviation﴾ — the Jews and the Christians, or the Magians, or the fornicators — ﴿that you should deviate with a great deviation﴾ — you would turn away from the truth by committing what has been forbidden to you, so that you would become like them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 28:

﴿Allah desires to lighten [the burden] for you﴾ He makes the rulings of the Sharia easy for you ﴿and man was created weak﴾ he cannot refrain from women and desires.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 29:

﴿O you who have believed, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly﴾ by what is forbidden in the sharia, such as usury (riba) and usurpation (ghasb), ﴿except﴾ but rather ﴿that it be a trade﴾ that it occur as ﴿a trade﴾. In another reading, with the accusative (tijaratan), it means: except that the wealth be wealth of trade, proceeding ﴿from mutual consent among you﴾ and goodwill of the soul; then you may consume it. ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾ by committing what leads to their destruction, whether in this world or the Hereafter, as indicated by ﴿indeed Allah is ever Merciful to you﴾ in His forbidding you from that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 30:

﴿And whoever does that﴾ i.e., what has been forbidden, ﴿in transgression﴾ going beyond what is lawful, (a circumstantial clause, ḥāl) ﴿and wrongdoing﴾ (an emphatic, ta'kīd) ﴿We will surely burn him﴾ We will cause him to enter ﴿in Fire﴾ in which he will be burned ﴿and that is for Allah ever easy﴾ light, effortless.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 31:

﴿If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden⦆ — these are those for which a threat has been stated, such as killing, fornication and theft. And it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that they are closer to seven hundred. ﴿We will remove from you your bad deeds⦆ — the minor sins — through acts of obedience. ﴿And We will admit you to an admission⦆ — read with a ḍammah and a fatḥah on the mīm — meaning an admission, or a place, ﴿noble⦆ — it is Paradise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 32:

﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you exceed others.﴾ That is, in worldly matters or in religion, lest it lead to envy and hatred. ﴿For men is a share﴾ meaning a reward ﴿of what they have earned﴾ by means of what they did, such as jihad and other things. ﴿And for women is a share of what they have earned﴾ from obeying their husbands and guarding their chastity. It was revealed when Umm Salamah said: "Would that we were men, so that we could fight and have a reward like the reward of men." ﴿And ask Allah of His bounty﴾ (the word is read with a hamzah and without it) ﴿what you need, and He will give it to you.﴾ ﴿Indeed Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾ From this comes the place of bounty and your asking.

﴿And for each﴾ of the men and the women, ﴿We have appointed heirs﴾, that is, ʿaṣaba (residuary kinsmen) who receive ﴿from what the parents and the close relatives leave﴾ of the wealth. ﴿And those with whom your oaths have bound you﴾ (ʿaqadat, read with an alif and without it) ﴿your oaths﴾, the plural of yamin, which means either an oath or a hand. That is, the allies with whom you made covenants in the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period) for mutual support and inheritance. ﴿Give them﴾ now ﴿their share﴾, their portions of the inheritance, which is one sixth. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Witness﴾, Observer, and nothing about your condition is hidden from Him. This ruling has been abrogated (naskh) by His words: ﴿And blood relatives are closer to one another﴾.

﴿Men are in charge of﴾ [i.e., have authority over (musallatun)] ﴿women﴾, disciplining them and restraining them from wrongdoing. ﴿Because Allah has made some of them excel over others﴾, meaning, by His giving them precedence over women in knowledge, intellect, guardianship and other matters. ﴿And because they spend of their wealth﴾ on them. ﴿So righteous women are obedient﴾ to their husbands, ﴿guarding in their absence what Allah has commanded them to guard﴾, meaning their chastity and other matters, in their husbands' absence, ﴿by what Allah has guarded﴾ for them, in that He has enjoined husbands to look after them. ﴿As for those women from whom you fear defiance﴾ (nushuz), meaning their disobedience to you, when its signs have appeared: ﴿admonish them﴾, that is, warn them of Allah; ﴿and forsake them in beds﴾, meaning withdraw to a separate bed if they show defiance; ﴿and strike them﴾ with a strike that is not severe, if they do not return through the forsaking. ﴿Then if they obey you﴾ in what is desired from them, ﴿seek no way against them﴾, meaning do not seek a pretext ﴿to strike them unjustly﴾. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Most High, Most Great﴾, so beware of Him lest He punish you if you wrong them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 35:

﴿And if you fear a breach﴾ you know (عَلِمْتُمْ) ﴿between the two﴾ a dissension (خِلاف) ﴿between them﴾ between the spouses; the annexation (al-idafa) is for expansiveness (li'l-ittisa'), i.e., a breach between them ﴿then send an arbiter﴾ to them, with their consent (بِرِضاهُما) ﴿a man of his family﴾ a just man (رَجُلًا عَدْلًا) ﴿from his family﴾ his relatives ﴿and an arbiter from her family﴾. The husband entrusts his arbiter with divorce and with accepting a compensation (عِوَض) from her for it, and she entrusts her arbiter with khul' (the wife's divorce by compensation). So the two arbiters exercise independent judgment (فَيَجْتَهِدانِ) and command the wrongdoer to return, or separate the two if they see that to be right. He, exalted is He, said ﴿If they both desire reconciliation﴾, i.e., the two arbiters (الحَكَمانِ), ﴿God will bring about harmony between them﴾ between the spouses, i.e., He will enable them to do what is obedience, of reconciliation or separation. ﴿Indeed, God is ever Knowing﴾ of everything, ﴿Acquainted﴾ with the inner matters as with the outward ones.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 36:

﴿Worship Allah﴾ — make Him one (tawhid); ﴿and associate nothing with Him﴾ — be good [to others]; ﴿and to parents, good treatment﴾ — kindness and lowering of the wing (of humility) [towards them]; ﴿and to the near of kin﴾ — the kinship; ﴿and orphans and the needy and the neighbour who is of kin﴾ — the one close to you by proximity or lineage; ﴿and the neighbour who is a stranger﴾ — the one far from you by proximity or lineage; ﴿and the companion by your side﴾ — the fellow traveller, or the colleague in a trade; and it is said, the wife; ﴿and the wayfarer﴾ — the one cut off on his journey; ﴿and those your right hands possess﴾ — of the slaves. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love those who are arrogant﴾ — proud; ﴿boastful﴾ — over the people, because of what He has given them.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 4, verse 37:

﴿Those who﴾ is the subject (mubtada'). ﴿Are stingy﴾ with what is obligatory upon them, ﴿and enjoin upon people stinginess﴾ with it, ﴿and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾ of knowledge and wealth. They are the Jews. The predicate (khabar) of the subject is: for them is a severe threat (wa'id shadid). ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers﴾ for that and for other than it ﴿a humiliating punishment﴾, meaning one that brings disgrace.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 38:

﴿Those who spend their wealth to be seen by people﴾ is conjoined to "those who" before it, [meaning they are] showing off to them. ﴿And they do not believe in Allah or the Last Day﴾ like the hypocrites and the people of Makkah. ﴿And whoever has Satan as his companion﴾ (qarin), a companion who acts by his command, like these [people], ﴿evil is he as a companion﴾ (fa-sa'a), meaning, wretched is he [as a companion].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 39:

﴿And what would it harm them, if they had believed in Allah and the Last Day and spent from what Allah has provided them?﴾ That is: what harm would there be upon them in that? The interrogative is for denial (al-inkar), and "law" (lau) is here a verbal particle (masdariyyah), meaning: there is no harm in it, and the harm lies only in what they are upon. ﴿And Allah was ever Knowing of them﴾, so He will recompense them for what they did.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 40:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong﴾ anyone ﴿even the weight of an atom﴾ (mithqal dharra), i.e., the weight of the smallest ant, by diminishing his good deeds or increasing his evil deeds. ﴿And if it is a good deed﴾, (i.e., if the atom is) a good deed from a believer, and in another reading it is read in the nominative (ḥasanatun), in which case kāna is complete (tāmmah), ﴿He multiplies it﴾ from ten up to more than seven hundred, and in another reading it is read yuḍaʿʿifhā with the doubled letter (tashdīd), ﴿and gives from Himself⁠﴾, from His presence, along with the multiplication, ﴿a great reward﴾ that no one can measure.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 4, verse 41:

﴿Then how (will it be)﴾ the condition of the disbelievers ﴿when We bring from every nation a witness﴾ who will testify against them concerning their deeds, and he is their prophet ﴿and We bring you, (O Muhammad), as a witness over these (people)﴾

﴿On that Day﴾, i.e., the Day of the Coming (of the Resurrection), ﴿those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish﴾ that ﴿they were leveled﴾. The verb ﴿تُسَوّى﴾ (*tusawwā*) is in the passive form (*bi'l-bināʾ lil-mafʿūl*, the passive voice), and it can also be read with the active sense. In the original it is *tatasawwā*, with one of the two tāʾs omitted and the other assimilated into the sīn. ﴿with them the earth﴾, meaning that they would become dust like it, because of the magnitude of its terror, as in another verse: ﴿And the disbeliever will say, "Would that I were dust!"﴾. ﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾ about what they did. At another time they will conceal it and say: ﴿"By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 43:

﴿O you who have believed, do not approach prayer﴾ i.e., do not pray ﴿while you are intoxicated﴾ from drink, because the occasion of its revelation was a congregational prayer performed while intoxicated ﴿until you know what you are saying﴾ by becoming sober ﴿nor [while you are] in a state of janabah﴾ by penetration or emission of semen; it is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), and it is applied to the singular and other than the singular ﴿except for passing through [it]﴾ crossing through ﴿a path﴾ a way, i.e., while travelling ﴿until you have washed⁠﴾ so then you may pray. The exception of the traveller is because he has a different ruling that will come later. It has also been said that what is meant is the prohibition of approaching the places of prayer, i.e., the mosques, except passing through them without staying ﴿And if you are ill﴾ with an illness that water harms ﴿or on a journey﴾ i.e., travelling, while you are in janabah or in a state of minor impurity ﴿or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself﴾ which is the place prepared for answering the call of nature, i.e., has passed wind ﴿or you have touched women﴾ and in one reading [it is] without the alif, and both mean touching, which is contact by the hand. This was said by Ibn ʿUmar, and al-Shafiʿi held this view, and contact with the rest of the skin has been added to it. From Ibn ʿAbbas: it is sexual intercourse ﴿and you do not find water﴾ with which to purify yourselves for prayer, after seeking and searching, and this refers to those other than the ill ﴿then perform tayammum﴾ intend, after the time has entered, ﴿clean earth﴾ pure dust, so strike it with two strikes ﴿and wipe your faces and your hands﴾ together with the elbows from it. Masaḥa is transitive by itself and by the particle.

﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion﴾ a share, ﴿of the Book﴾ and they are the Jews, ﴿they buy error﴾ in exchange for guidance, ﴿and they want you to lose the way﴾ you to miss the true path, ﴿so that you become like them.﴾

Allah knows best your enemies, [better than you do] — so He informs you about them, that you may avoid them. "And sufficient is Allah as a Protector (waliyy)" — guarding you from them. "And sufficient is Allah as a Helper (nasir)" — preventing them from plotting against you.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 46:

﴿Among those who are Jews﴾ are a people ﴿who distort﴾ (yuharrifuna), i.e., change ﴿the words﴾ (al-kalim) ﴿from their places﴾ (ʿan mawadiʿihi) ﴾; the words which God revealed in the Torah concerning the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿from their places﴾ where they were placed. ﴿And they say﴾ to the Prophet (ﷺ), when he commands them to do something: ﴿"We hear"﴾ your speech, ﴿"and we disobey"﴾ your command. ﴿"Hear, but not heard"﴾, a circumstantial phrase carrying the sense of a supplication, meaning: may you never hear. ﴿And﴾ they say to him: ﴿"Ra'ina"﴾ (Ra'ina), although he was forbidden to address him with it, and it is a word of abuse in their language. ﴿Twisting﴾ (layyan) means distorting ﴿with their tongues﴾ and ﴿slandering﴾ (ta'nan), meaning disparaging, ﴿the religion﴾, which is Islam. ﴿If only they had said: "We hear and we obey"﴾ instead of "we disobey", ﴿"and hear"﴾ alone, ﴿"and look at us"﴾, meaning: "look upon us", instead of "Ra'ina", ﴿it would have been better for them﴾ than what they said ﴿and more upright﴾, more just than it. ﴿But God has cursed them﴾, i.e., removed them far from His mercy, ﴿for their disbelief. So they do not believe, except a few﴾ of them, such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and his companions.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 47:

﴿O you who were given the Book, believe in what We have sent down﴾ of the Qur'an, ﴿confirming what is with you﴾ of the Torah, ﴿before We obliterate faces﴾ by erasing what is in them of eyes, nose and brows, ﴿and turn them back on their backs﴾ by making them like the nape, one flat surface, ﴿or curse them﴾ by transforming them into apes, ﴿as We cursed the companions of the Sabbath﴾ — We transformed some of them — ﴿and the command of God is ever accomplished﴾ — His decree is carried out. ﴿And when it was revealed, ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām embraced Islam.﴾ It was said that it was a threat conditional upon something, and when some of them embraced Islam, it was lifted. It was also said that the obliteration and transformation will occur before the Hour.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 48:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾, i.e., shirk (associating partners with Allah), ﴿but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾, i.e., other sins besides that, ﴿for whom He wills﴾ forgiveness, by admitting him into Paradise without punishment; and whoever He wills of the believers He punishes for his sins, then admits him into Paradise. ﴿And whoever associates partners with Allah has indeed fabricated a sin﴾, i.e., committed a sin, ﴿great﴾, i.e., grave.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 49:

﴿Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves?﴾ They are the Jews, when they said: "We are the children of God and His beloved ones." That is, the matter is not as they claim by praising themselves. ﴿Rather, God purifies whom He wills﴾ (yuṭahhir), through faith. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ (yunqaṣūn), that is, they will not have any of their deeds reduced ﴿even by a fatil﴾, the amount of the thin thread on the skin of a date-stone.
﴿Look﴾, in wonder, ﴿at how they fabricate lies against God﴾ by that, ﴿and that suffices as a manifest sin﴾, clear.

The revelation came concerning Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and others like him from among the scholars of the Jews, when they came to Makkah, saw the slain of Badr, and incited the polytheists to take revenge for them and to wage war against the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They believe in al-Jibt and at-Taghut﴾ — two idols of the Quraysh. ﴿And they say to those who disbelieve﴾ — Abu Sufyan and his companions, when they said to them: "Are we better guided than Muhammad in the way? We are the custodians of the House, we give drink to the pilgrims, we host the guest, we free the captive, and we do (all this), whereas Muhammad has opposed the religion of his forefathers, severed the ties of kinship, and departed from the Sacred Precinct?" ﴿These﴾, that is, you, ﴿are better guided in the way than those who believe﴾, more upright in path.
﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, and whoever Allah curses, you will not find for him a helper﴾ preventing him from His punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 53:

﴿Am﴾ (Or) rather, ﴿for them is a share in the dominion﴾, i.e., they have no share of it at all. And even if they did, ﴿then they would not give the people even a speck﴾, i.e., anything trivial, the size of the pit in the back of a date-stone, because of their extreme stinginess.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 54:

﴿Am﴾ (rather) ﴿do they envy the people﴾ i.e., the Prophet (ﷺ) ﴿for what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾ of prophethood and the abundance of wives; i.e., they wish his blessing would cease from him, and they say, "If he were a prophet, he would have been occupied away from women." ﴿Indeed, We gave the family of Abraham﴾ his forefather, such as Moses, David and Solomon, ﴿the Book and wisdom﴾ and prophethood, ﴿and We gave them a great kingdom﴾. So David had ninety-nine wives, and Solomon had a thousand, between free women and concubines.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 55:

﴿Among them are those who believed in him﴾ in Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿and among them are those who turned away from him﴾ i.e., turned away from him and did not believe. ﴿And Hell is sufficient as a blazing fire﴾ as a punishment for those who do not believe.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 56:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved in Our signs – We will surely burn them in Fire﴾ – We will cause them to enter a Fire ﴿in which they will burn. Whenever their skins are roasted﴾ – were burned ﴿We will exchange them for other skins﴾ – by returning them to their former state, not burned ﴿so they may taste the punishment﴾ – so that they will experience its severity. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted in Might﴾ – nothing can overpower Him ﴿Wise﴾ – in His creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 57:

﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds – We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever.﴾ "Forever therein for them" ﴿spouses purified﴾ from menstruation and every impurity. ﴿And We will admit them to a shade, extending⁠﻿﻿ — ﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿...

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 4, verse 58:**

﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render the trusts to their owners﴾, meaning: what has been entrusted to you of rights, ﴿to those entitled to them﴾. It was revealed when ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, took the key of the Kaaba by force from ʿUthman ibn Talhah al-Hajabi, its keeper (sadin), when the Prophet (ﷺ) entered Makkah in the year of the Conquest. He (ʿUthman) refused him and said: "Had I known that he was the Messenger of Allah, I would not have refused him." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded that it be returned to him, and said: "Take it, [it is] everlasting and inherited." He (ʿUthman) was amazed at this, so ʿAli recited the verse to him, and he embraced Islam. [The Prophet] gave it to him at his death, and he gave it to his brother Shaybah, and it remained in his descendants. The verse, although it was revealed concerning a specific occasion, its generality is taken into account by the context of the plural.

﴿And when you judge between people﴾, He commands you ﴿to judge with justice. Indeed, Allah is excellent [in what] He admonishes you with﴾. In it there is idghām (assimilation) of the mīm of نِعْمَ (niʿma) into ما (mā), the indefinite mā being a descriptive (nakirah mawsufah, an indefinite qualified noun), meaning نِعْمَ شَيْئًا (niʿma shayʾan), "an excellent thing." ﴿He admonishes you with it﴾, namely, the rendering of the trust and judging with justice. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever All-Hearing﴾ of what is said, ﴿All-Seeing﴾ of what is done.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 59:

﴿O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority (ulu al-amr) among you﴾ — ﴿those in authority﴾ means the rulers (al-wulat), ﴿among you﴾ — provided they command you to obey Allah and His Messenger. ﴿And if you dispute over anything﴾ — you differ, ﴿refer it to Allah﴾ — that is, to His Book, ﴿and the Messenger﴾ — during his lifetime, and after him to his Sunnah; that is, seek clarification from these two regarding it. ﴿If you should believe in Allah and the Last Day. That﴾ — that is, referring it to them, ﴿is better﴾ — for you than disputing and speaking by opinion (al-qawl bil-ra'y), ﴿and better in outcome﴾ — in result (ma'alan).

It was revealed when a Jew and a hypocrite (munafiq) quarreled. The hypocrite called for them to take the matter to Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf so that he would judge between them, while the Jew called for them to take it to the Prophet (ﷺ). So they both went to him, and he ruled in favor of the Jew, but the hypocrite was not content. They then went to ʿUmar, and the Jew told him of that. ʿUmar said to the hypocrite, "Is it so?" He said, "Yes," so ʿUmar killed him.

﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet they desire to take their disputes to the false deity (al-ṭāghūt)?﴾ The ṭāghūt is one who exceeds all bounds in transgression, and it is Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf. ﴿And they were commanded to reject it﴾ and not to take it as an ally. ﴿And Satan desires to lead them far astray﴾ from the truth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 61:

﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has sent down,"﴾ in the Qur'an of judgment, ﴿and to the Messenger,﴾ that he may judge between you, ﴿you see the hypocrites turning away﴾ from, ﴿away from you﴾ toward others.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 62:

﴿Then how﴾ will they act ﴿when a calamity befalls them﴾ as a punishment ﴿for what their hands have sent ahead﴾ of disbelief and sins? That is, can they avoid it and flee from it? No. ﴿Then they come to you﴾ is conjoined to "they turn away" (yaṣuddūna). ﴿Swearing by Allah: "We intended nothing﴾ by seeking judgment from other than you ﴿but good﴾ reconciliation ﴿and conciliation﴾ (tawfīq), that is, bringing the two adversaries together by seeking closeness in the ruling, without pushing them toward the bitterness of the truth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 63:

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah knows what is in their hearts﴾ of hypocrisy and their lying in their excuse. ﴿So turn away from them﴾ by pardoning them. ﴿And admonish them﴾ — frighten them with Allah. ﴿And say to them concerning﴾ their own selves ﴿a far-reaching word﴾ affecting them; that is, rebuke them so that they may return from their disbelief.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 64:

﴿And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed﴾ in what he commands and judges, ﴿by the leave of Allah﴾ by His command, not to be disobeyed and opposed. ﴿And if, when they had wronged themselves﴾ by resorting to the judgment of the tyrant (al-Taghut), ﴿they had come to you﴾ repentant, ﴿and asked Allah's forgiveness, and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them﴾ – here there is a shift from address (iltifat) ʿan al-khitab, to magnify his status – ﴿they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance﴾ toward them, ﴿Merciful﴾ to them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 65:

﴿So no, by your Lord﴾ the "lā" is extra (zā'ida), ﴿they will not believe until they make you judge in what has become confused among them﴾ meaning, got mixed up, ﴿then they do not find within themselves any discomfort﴾ meaning, constriction, or doubt ﴿concerning what you have decided﴾ with it, ﴿and submit﴾ meaning, yield ﴿to your judgment, in full submission﴾ without any objection.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 66:

﴿Had We prescribed for them, "Kill yourselves or leave your homes,"﴾ [an (أن) here is explanatory (mufassirah)] ﴿as We prescribed for the Children of Israel, they would not have done it,﴾ i.e., what was prescribed for them, ﴿except a few of them.﴾ [Qalil is read in the nominative (bi-al-raf') as a substitute (badal), and in the accusative (al-nasb) as an exception (istithna').] ﴿But if they had done what they were admonished to do,﴾ of obedience to the Messenger (ﷺ), ﴿it would have been better for them and firmer in establishing [their faith]﴾ i.e., more certain in confirming their faith.
﴿And then﴾ meaning: if they had remained steadfast, ﴿We would have given them from Us﴾ from Our presence ﴿a great reward﴾ which is Paradise.

﴿And We would have guided them to a straight path.﴾ Some of the Companions said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "How will we see you in Paradise when you are in the high ranks and we are below you?" So it was revealed.

﴿Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger﴾ in what he commands, ﴿those are with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, of the prophets and the ṣiddīqūn (the foremost truthful ones)﴾, meaning the most distinguished companions of the prophets, because of their great truthfulness and their affirmation of the truth, ﴿and the martyrs﴾, meaning those slain in the way of Allah, ﴿and the righteous﴾, other than those already mentioned. ﴿And excellent companions are they﴾: "رُفَقاء" (rufaqāʾ, companions) in Paradise, whereby one enjoys in it seeing them, visiting them, and being in their presence, even though their abode is in higher ranks compared to others.

﴿That﴾, i.e., their being with those mentioned, is a subject (mubtada', the grammatical subject) whose predicate (khabar, the grammatical predicate) is ﴿the bounty from Allah﴾, which He bestowed upon them, not that they attained it through their obedience. ﴿And Allah suffices as Knower﴾ of the reward of the Hereafter, i.e., so trust what He has informed you of. ﴿And none will inform you like one who is All-Aware﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 71:

﴿O you who have believed, take your precaution﴾ from your enemy, i.e., be cautious of him and be alert to him. ﴿Then go forth [in companies]﴾ rise up to fight him ﴿in companies﴾ dispersed, a detachment after another ﴿or go forth all together﴾ gathered together.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 72:

﴿And indeed, among you is one who will certainly lag behind﴾ he will hold back from fighting, like ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy the hypocrite and his companions; and his being counted among you is on the basis of outward appearance; and the lām in the verb is the lām of oath (lam al-qasam). ﴿So if a calamity befalls you﴾ such as being killed or defeated, ﴿he says: "Allah has blessed me, since I was not present with them as a witness﴾ present (ḥāḍiran), so that I was not struck (fa-uṣība)."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 73:

﴿And if there should befall you a bounty from Allah﴾ — the lam here is the lam of oath (lam al-qasam) — such as a conquest and spoils of war, ﴿he will surely say﴾ regretfully, ﴿as if﴾ (kaʾan, here the light form, kaʾanna) ﴿there had never been﴾ — with the yaʾ and the taʾ (both readings: yakun and takun) — ﴿between you and him any affection﴾, i.e. acquaintance and friendship. This refers back to his saying "Allah has certainly blessed me" (qad anʿama Allah ʿalayya). He interposed this between the speech and its statement, which is ﴿O﴾ (ya, an particle of alerting, tanbih) ﴿would that I had been with them, so I would have achieved a great achievement﴾, i.e. I would have taken a large share of the spoils of war.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 74:

﴿So let those fight in the way of Allah﴾ for the elevation of His religion, ﴿who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter⁠﴾ — who sell (يَبِيعُونَ, yabī'ūn) ﴿the life of this world for the Hereafter. And whoever fights in the way of Allah, and is killed﴾ — is martyred ﴿or overcomes﴾ — gains victory over his enemy ﴿We will give him a great reward﴾ — an abundant reward.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 75:

﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the cause of Allah﴾. This is an interrogative of reproach, meaning: there is nothing preventing you from fighting ﴿in the cause of Allah﴾, and in [the cause of] rescuing ﴿the oppressed men, women, and children﴾ who were held back by the disbelievers from emigrating (hijrah) and who harmed them. Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I and my mother were among them." ﴿Who say﴾ supplicating, "﴿Our Lord, bring us out of this city﴾" — Makkah — ﴿whose people are wrongdoers﴾ through disbelief, ﴿and appoint for us from Yourself﴾ from Your presence ﴿a protector﴾ who will manage our affairs, ﴿and appoint for us from Yourself a helper﴾ who will protect us from them. Allah answered their supplication: He made it easy for some of them to go out, while some of them remained until Makkah was conquered. The Prophet (ﷺ) appointed ʿAttab ibn Asid, and he gave the oppressed among them justice against their oppressor.

﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of God, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the false deity (al-Ṭāghūt)﴾, meaning Satan, ﴿so fight the allies of Satan﴾, meaning the supporters of his religion. You will overcome them through your strength in God. ﴿Indeed, the plot of Satan﴾ against the believers ﴿was ever weak﴾, feeble and unable to withstand, whereas the plot of God against the disbelievers cannot be resisted.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 4, verse 77:

﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands"﴾ from fighting the disbelievers, when they asked for permission to fight them in Makkah because the disbelievers were harming them. They were a group of the Companions (al-Sahabah). ﴿"And establish the prayer and give the zakat." But when fighting was prescribed﴾ (furidha) ﴿for them, behold, a party of them fear﴾ (yakhafun) ﴿men﴾, that is, the disbelievers, meaning their punishment by killing, ﴿as they fear﴾ the punishment of ﴿Allah, or with a greater fear﴾ than their fear of them. The word ﴿ashadda﴾ (greater) is in the accusative (nasb) as a circumstantial accusative (hal), and its response (jawab) is what is implied by ﴿idha﴾ (when) and what follows it, meaning: fear overtook them. ﴿And they said﴾, out of dread of death, ﴿"Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only﴾ (lawla, meaning "why not" or "would that") ﴿You had delayed us to a near term."﴾ Say to them: ﴿"The enjoyment of this world﴾ is what one enjoys in it, or the enjoyment of it, ﴿is little﴾, tending toward extinction. ﴿And the Hereafter﴾, that is, Paradise, ﴿is better for him who fears﴾ the punishment of ﴿Allah, by avoiding His disobedience. ﴿And you will not be wronged﴾ with the ta' and with the ya' (two readings: the first addressing "you," the second "they"), ﴿a whit﴾ — you will not have any of your deeds diminished ﴿of your deeds﴾, ﴿the amount of a fatil﴾ (the thin thread in the split of a date-stone). ﴿So fight﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 78:

﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are in towers built up high﴾ fortresses ﴿built up high﴾ lofty. So do not fear fighting out of fear of death. ﴿And if good befalls them﴾ i.e., the Jews, ﴿good﴾ fertility and abundance, ﴿they say, "This is from Allah." And if evil befalls them﴾ drought and calamity, as happened to them when the Prophet ﷺ arrived in Madinah, ﴿they say, "This is from you﴾ O Muhammad, i.e., because of your ill omen." ﴿Say﴾ to them, ﴿"All﴾ of the good and the evil ﴿is from Allah,"﴾ from Him. ﴿So what is wrong with these people, that they hardly understand any statement﴾ i.e., they hardly come close to understanding ﴿a statement﴾ that is conveyed to them? The interrogative here is an expression of wonder at their extreme ignorance, and negating the approach of the act is stronger than negating the act itself.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 79:

﴿Whatever good befalls you﴾, O human being, ﴿is from Allah﴾, i.e., it has come to you as a bounty from Him, ﴿and whatever evil befalls you﴾, i.e., an affliction, ﴿is from yourself﴾, i.e., it has come to you because of what you committed of sins that deserve it. ﴿And We have sent you, O Muhammad, as a messenger to mankind﴾, a emphasizing circumstantial clause (ḥāl muʾakkida). ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾ to your message.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 80:

﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah; but whoever turns away—﴾ turns away from your obedience, so do not let it trouble you. ﴿We have not sent you as a guardian over them.﴾ A guardian over their deeds; rather you are only a warner. And their affair is up to Us, so We will requite them. And this was before the command to fight.

**(Tafsir al-Jalalayn)**, commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti on Surah al-Nisa', verse 81:

﴿And they say﴾, i.e., the hypocrites: when they come to you, "We are commanded to ﴿obedience﴾" to you. ﴿But when they go out﴾, i.e., leave ﴿from your presence, a group of them plots﴾ (بَيَّتَ, read with the assimilation of the tā' into the ṭā', and also without assimilation), i.e., they harbour ﴿other than what you say﴾ to you in your presence of obedience, i.e., their disobedience. ﴿But Allah records﴾, i.e., orders the recording of ﴿what they plot﴾ in their records, so that they may be recompensed for it. ﴿So turn away from them﴾ by pardoning them. ﴿And rely upon Allah﴾, i.e., trust in Him, for He is sufficient for you. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾, i.e., one to whom affairs are entrusted.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 82:

﴿Will they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?﴾ (yatadabbaruna) they ponder over (yata'ammaluna) ﴿the Qur'an﴾ and its wondrous meanings. ﴿Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy﴾: contradiction in its meanings and incongruity in its composition.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 83:

﴿And when there comes to them a matter﴾ concerning the military expeditions (sarāyā) of the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding what has happened to them, ﴿of security﴾ through victory, ﴿or fear﴾ through defeat, ﴿they spread it abroad﴾, meaning they divulged it. It was revealed concerning a group of the hypocrites, or concerning the weak among the believers, who used to do this, thereby weakening the hearts of the believers and causing the Prophet (ﷺ) distress. ﴿But if they had referred it﴾, i.e. the report, ﴿to the Messenger and to those in authority among them﴾, i.e. those of judgment among the senior Companions (al-ṣaḥābah), meaning if they had kept silent about it until they were informed of it, ﴿they would have known it﴾, whether it is something that should be spread or not, ﴿those who seek to draw it out﴾, i.e. who follow it up and seek knowledge of it, and they are the ones who spread it, ﴿from among them﴾, from among the Messenger and those in authority. ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you﴾ through Islam ﴿and His mercy﴾ upon you through the Qur'an, ﴿you would have followed Satan﴾ in what he commands you of indecencies.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 84:

﴿So fight﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿in the way of Allah. You are not burdened except with yourself﴾, so do not concern yourself with their staying behind from you. The meaning: fight, even if alone, for you are promised victory. ﴿And urge the believers﴾ exhort them to fighting and encourage them towards it. ﴿It may be that Allah will restrain the might﴾ the fighting ﴿of those who disbelieve. And Allah is greater in might﴾ than them ﴿and greater in punishment﴾ torment than them. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, I will go out even if I am alone." So he went out with seventy riders to Badr al-Sughra (the Lesser Badr), and Allah restrained the might of the disbelievers by casting terror into their hearts, and He prevented Abu Sufyan from going out, as has preceded in Surat Al 'Imran.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 85:

﴿Whoever intercedes﴾ between people ﴿with a good intercession﴾ (one conforming to the Shari'ah), ﴿he will have a share﴾ of the reward ﴿from it﴾, by means of it. ﴿And whoever intercedes with a bad intercession﴾ (one opposing it), ﴿he will have a portion﴾ (kifl) (a share of the burden) ﴿from it﴾, by means of it. ﴿And Allah is ever Ruler over all things﴾ (muqtadir), so He will recompense every person for what he has done.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 86:

﴿And when you are greeted with a greeting﴾, as if it were said to you, "Peace be upon you," ﴿then greet﴾ the one who greets you ﴿with something better than it﴾, by saying to him, "And upon you be peace, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings," ﴿or return it﴾ by saying to him the same as he said. That is, the obligation is one of the two, and the first (the better greeting) is more excellent. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Ever Reckoning﴾, Taking account, so He will recompense for it, and among it is returning the greeting. The Sunnah has made exceptions to this: the disbeliever, the innovator, the wicked person, the one who greets someone relieving himself, the one in the bathhouse, and the one eating; so it is not obligatory to return the greeting to them, but it is disliked, except in the last case. It is said that to the disbeliever one says, "And upon you."

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on Surah 4, verse 87:

﴿Allah, there is no deity except Him﴾. And by Allah, ﴿He will surely gather you﴾ from your graves ﴿to﴾ in ﴿the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt﴾, no uncertainty. ﴿And who is more truthful than Allah in statement﴾, i.e., no one is more truthful than Allah in speech (qawlan).

When some people returned from Uhud, the people disagreed about them. One group said, "Kill them," and another group said, "No." So this was revealed: ﴿So what is the matter with you that you have become two groups concerning the hypocrites?﴾ (i.e., what is your state, that you have become two factions) ﴿And Allah has reverted them﴾ (i.e., returned them) ﴿for what they have earned﴾ of disbelief and sins. ﴿Do you wish to guide those whom Allah has sent astray? And whoever Allah sends astray, you will not find for him any way﴾ (i.e., do you count them among those who are guided? The interrogative in both places is for denial) ﴿for him any way﴾ (a path) to guidance.

They desire that you disbelieve as they have disbelieved, [so] that you would be equal [to them]. So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate in the cause of Allah. But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them, and do not take from among them an ally or a helper.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on surah 4, verse 90:

﴿Except those who take refuge﴾ (yasilun) seek refuge ﴿with a people between you and them is a covenant﴾ ('ahd, a pact of safe-conduct) for them, and for whoever joins them, as Hilal ibn 'Uwaymir al-Aslami made a covenant with the Prophet (ﷺ) ﴿or﴾ those who ﴿come to you﴾ and ﴿their hearts are constricted﴾ (hasirat, i.e., straitened) ﴿from fighting you﴾ alongside their own people ﴿or fighting their own people﴾ alongside you, meaning, refraining from fighting both you and them; so do not confront them by taking or killing them. This and what follows it ﴿is abrogated﴾ (mansukh) by the verse of the sword.

﴿And if God had willed﴾ to give them power over you ﴿He would have given them power over you﴾ by strengthening their hearts ﴿so they would have fought you﴾. But He did not will it, and so He cast terror into their hearts. ﴿But if they withdraw from you and do not fight you, and offer you peace﴾ (al-salam, reconciliation), meaning, submit to you, ﴿then God has not given you any way﴾ (sabilan, a path) against them, by taking or killing them.

You will find others who wish to be secure from you by displaying faith in your presence, and [wish] to be secure from their own people by [displaying] disbelief when they return to them, namely Asad and Ghatafan. Every time they are sent back to temptation, they are cast into it headlong: they are called to *shirk* (associating partners with God), and they fall into it in the worst possible way. If they do not withdraw from you by ceasing to fight you, and do not offer you *salam* (peace), and do not restrain their hands from you, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them. Against them We have given you a clear authority, a manifest and evident proof for killing them and taking them captive because of their treachery.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 92:

﴿It is not for a believer to kill a believer﴾ meaning: it is not befitting that killing should proceed from him against him, ﴿except by mistake﴾ (being) mistaken in his killing, without intent. ﴿And whoever kills a believer by mistake﴾ such as by intending to strike someone else, like game or a tree, and hitting him, or striking him with something that does not usually kill, ﴿then (he must free) a believing slave﴾ a soul (nasamah) upon him, ﴿and a compensation (diyah) paid over﴾ handed over ﴿to his family﴾ meaning the heirs of the one killed, ﴿unless they remit it﴾ they give it up as charity to him, by forgoing it. The Sunnah has clarified that it is one hundred camels: twenty bint makhad, likewise bint labun, ibn labun, hiqqah and jidha'. It is borne by the relatives of the killer (ʿaqilah), who are his agnatic kin in the ascending and descending line, distributed upon them over three years: upon the wealthy among them half a dinar, and upon the middling a quarter, each year. If they cannot meet it, then from the treasury (bayt al-mal). If that is impossible, then upon the offender himself. ﴿If he was﴾ the one killed ﴿from a people hostile to you﴾ at war with you, ﴿and he was a believer, then (the penalty is) freeing a believing slave﴾ upon his killer as an expiation (kaffarah), and no compensation is handed over to his family, because they are at war. ﴿And if he was﴾ the one killed ﴿from a people between you and them is a covenant﴾ a treaty, such as the people of the dhimmah, ﴿then a compensation is due to him, handed over to his family﴾, and it is one-third of the diyah of a believer if he was a Jew or a Christian, and two-thirds of a tenth of it if he was a Magian. ﴿And freeing a believing slave﴾ upon his killer. ﴿But whoever does not find﴾ a slave, by being unable to obtain him and what would procure him, ﴿then fasting two consecutive months﴾ is upon him as an expiation. God Most High did not mention moving on to feeding, as in the case of zihar, and al-Shafi'i adopted this in his more correct of two opinions. ﴿A repentance from God﴾ an infinitive verbal noun in the accusative, governed by its implied verb. ﴿And God is ever Knowing﴾ of His creation, ﴿Wise﴾ in what He has ordained for them.

﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally﴾ by intending to kill him with what usually kills, ﴿his recompense is Hell, abiding therein; and Allah is angry with him and has cursed him﴾, that is, removed him far from His mercy, ﴿and has prepared for him a great punishment﴾ in the Fire. This is interpreted as referring to one who deems it lawful (yastahilluhu), or as meaning that this is his recompense if he is requited, and there is no oddity in the non-fulfilment of the threat, due to His saying ﴿and He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills﴾. It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas that it is to be taken in its apparent sense, and that it is abrogating (nāsikha, from naskh, abrogation) of other verses about forgiveness. The verse of al-Baqarah explained that the one who kills intentionally is to be killed in retaliation (qiṣāṣ) for it, and that he owes the blood-money (diyya) if the victim's family pardons him, and its amount has already been mentioned. The Sunnah explained that between intentional and accidental killing there is a killing called shibh al-ʿamd (semi-intentional killing), which is to kill him with what does not usually kill; there is no retaliation in it, but rather blood-money, like intentional killing in its description and like accidental killing in its deferral and bearing (by the paternal kin). And intentional killing is more deserving of expiation (kaffāra) than accidental killing.

It was revealed when a group of the Companions (al-Ṣaḥābah) passed by a man from the Banu Sulaym who was driving a flock of sheep. He greeted them with salam, but they said, "He only greeted us out of taqiyyah (precautionary dissimulation)," so they killed him and seized his sheep. ﴿O you who have believed, when you go forth⁠﴾ to fight in the jihad (struggle, here military campaign), ﴿in the cause of Allah, investigate carefully⁠﴾. In another recitation (qirā'ah), it is read as fa-tathabbatū in both places. ﴿And do not say to one who gives you [the greeting of] peace⁠﴾ with the word al-salām (السَّلام), with an alif or without it, meaning the greeting or the submission by the words of testimony that are a sign of Islam, ﴿"You are not a believer⁠﴾. You only said this out of taqiyyah for your own self and property, so that you would kill him. ﴿You seek⁠﴾ you seek by that ﴿the goods of worldly life⁠﴾ its wealth from the spoils (ghanīmah). ﴿But with Allah are abundant spoils⁠﴾ which will make you independent of killing such a man for his property. ﴿Thus you were before⁠﴾ your blood and property were protected merely by your saying the testimony. ﴿Then Allah conferred favor upon you⁠﴾ by becoming well known for faith and steadfastness. ﴿So investigate carefully⁠﴾ lest you kill a believer, and deal with the one who has entered Islam as you were dealt with. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted⁠﴾, so He will reward you for it.

﴿Those who sit back among the believers, other than those with a harm,﴾ from jihad. ﴿"Other than those with a harm"﴾ is read in the nominative (*al-raf'*) as a qualifier (*sifah*), and in the accusative (*al-nasb*) as an exception (*istithna'*), from among those with chronic illness (*zamanah*), blindness or the like. ﴿And those who strive in the way of God with their wealth and their lives are not equal﴾ to those who sit back. ﴿God has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit back﴾ because of a harm, ﴿by a degree﴾, meaning a virtue, because the two are equal in intention (*niyyah*), and the strivers have an added merit through direct participation (*mubashara*). ﴿To each﴾ of the two groups ﴿God has promised the best reward﴾, meaning Paradise. ﴿But God has preferred those who strive over those who sit back﴾ without a harm ﴿with a great reward﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 96:

﴿Degrees from Him﴾: ranks, some above others, in honour. ﴿And forgiveness and mercy﴾: the words مَغْفِرَة and رَحْمَة are both in the accusative (manṣūbān), governed by their own implied verb (fi'luhumā al-muqaddar). ﴿And Allah was ever Forgiving﴾ toward His friends (awliyā'ihi), ﴿Merciful﴾ toward the people of His obedience (ahl ṭā'atihi).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 97:

﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves﴾ by remaining among the disbelievers and abandoning the emigration (hijrah). It was revealed concerning a group who embraced Islam but did not emigrate, and so they were killed at the Battle of Badr alongside the disbelievers. ﴿The angels will say﴾ to them, rebuking them: ﴿"In what condition were you?"﴾ i.e., in what matter of your religion were you? ﴿They will say﴾ by way of excuse: ﴿"We were oppressed (mustad'afin) in the land"﴾ i.e., unable to establish the religion ﴿"in the land"﴾ meaning the land of Makkah. ﴿They will say﴾ to them in reproach: ﴿"Was not the earth of Allah spacious, so that you could have emigrated therein?"﴾ from the land of disbelief to another country, as your best (of them) did. ﴿So their refuge is Hell, and evil is it as a destination﴾ — it is...

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 98:

﴿Except the oppressed among men, women and children﴾ who ﴿are unable to devise a plan﴾, who have no strength to emigrate and no provision, ﴿nor are they able to find a way﴾, a path to the land of emigration.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 100:

﴿And whoever emigrates in the way of Allah will find on the earth many a refuge and abundance﴾ [i.e., a migrant] ﴿many﴾ [and] ﴿abundance﴾ in provision. ﴿And whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger, and then death overtakes him﴾ on the way, as happened to Jundaʿ ibn Ḍamra al-Laythi, ﴿his reward is already due﴾ [i.e., it is established].

﴿And when you travel﴾ (sāfartum) through the earth, ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾ in ﴿shortening the prayer﴾ by reducing it from four [units] to two, ﴿if you fear that the disbelievers may afflict you﴾, i.e., may reach you with harm. ﴿The disbelievers﴾ is an explanation of the actual situation at that time, so it has no implied restriction (mafhūm, an implied meaning that would limit the ruling). The Sunnah (the Prophetic tradition) has clarified that the intended travel is a long journey, which is four barīd (a unit of distance), and these are two marhalatan (stages of travel). It is derived from His saying, ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾, that it is a rukhsa (concession) and not a wājib (obligation), and al-Shāfi'ī held this view. ﴿Indeed the disbelievers have been to you an evident enemy﴾, i.e., clearly hostile.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 4, verse 102:

﴿And when you are among them﴾, O Muhammad, present ﴿among them﴾, and they fear the enemy, ﴿and you establish the prayer for them﴾. This is a continuation of the Qur'an's customary mode of address. ﴿Let one group of them stand with you﴾, while another group holds back, ﴿and let them take their weapons﴾, meaning the group that stood with you, ﴿with them﴾. ﴿Then when they have prostrated﴾, meaning prayed, ﴿let them be﴾, meaning the other group, ﴿behind you﴾, guarding you until you finish the prayer, and this group goes off to guard. ﴿Then let another group come who have not prayed, and let them pray with you, and let them take their precaution and their weapons﴾ with them, until you finish the prayer. The Prophet (ﷺ) did this at Batn Nakhl, as narrated by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim). ﴿The disbelievers wish that you would be negligent﴾ when you go to the prayer ﴿of your weapons and your belongings, so they could attack you in a single assault﴾, by charging at you and seizing you. This is the reason for the command to take up weapons. ﴿And there is no blame upon you if there is discomfort from rain or if you are ill, that you lay down your weapons﴾, so you do not carry them.
