This indicates that carrying them is obligatory when there is no excuse, and this is one of two opinions of al-Shafi'i; the second is that it is recommended (sunnah), and this view was preferred. ﴿And take your precaution﴾ against the enemy, meaning guard yourselves against them as much as you can. ﴿Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾, one bringing disgrace.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 103:

﴿So when you have finished the prayer﴾ i.e., completed it, ﴿remember Allah﴾ with tahlil (saying "la ilaha illa Allah") and tasbih (saying "subhan Allah"), ﴿standing, sitting, and on your sides﴾ i.e., lying down, meaning in every state. ﴿So when you are secure﴾ i.e., safe, ﴿establish the prayer﴾ perform it with its due rights. ﴿Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers as a decree with specified times﴾ i.e., written, meaning obligatory, ﴿with specified times﴾ i.e., its time is fixed, so it is not to be delayed beyond it.

It was revealed when the Prophet (ﷺ) sent a company in pursuit of Abu Sufyan and his companions, after they had returned from Uhud, and they complained of their wounds.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 104:

﴿And do not weaken﴾ (lit. do not become feeble, tatha'ufu) ﴿in pursuit of the people﴾ (i.e., seeking out the disbelievers) to fight them ﴿if you suffer pain﴾ (i.e., you find the pain of wounds) ﴿then they too suffer pain as you suffer pain﴾ (i.e., like you), and they do not shrink from fighting you. ﴿But you hope﴾ (i.e., you) ﴿from Allah﴾ (i.e., victory and the reward for it) ﴿for what they do not hope﴾ (i.e., they). So you have an advantage over them in this, and so you should be more eager for it than they are. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing﴾ (of everything) ﴿Wise﴾ (in His creation).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 4, verse 105:

And Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq stole a coat of mail (dir'an) and hid it with a Jew, and it was found in his possession. Ṭu'ma threw it off onto him and swore that he had not stolen it. So his people asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to argue on his behalf and clear him, and there was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book﴾, the Qur'an, ﴿with the truth﴾, related to "sent down", ﴿that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, that is, what He has made you know concerning it, ﴿and do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾, like Ṭu'ma, ﴿a disputant﴾, one who argues on their behalf.
﴿And ask Allah for forgiveness﴾ for what you had inclined toward.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 107:

﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾ they betray themselves by sins, because the harm of their betrayal falls upon them ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is constantly treacherous﴾ abundant in betrayal ﴿sinful﴾ i.e., He will punish him.

﴿They hide﴾ i.e., Ṭu'ma and his people, out of shame ﴿from people, yet they cannot hide from Allah, when He is with them﴾ by His knowledge ﴿when they plot﴾ they conceal ﴿what He does not approve of in speech﴾ from their resolve to swear an oath denying the theft and to throw it upon the Jew ﴿and Allah is ever encompassing﴾ in knowledge ﴿of what they do﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 109:

﴿Here you are﴾, O ﴿you﴾ — an address to the people of Ṭu'ma (Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq, whose kinsmen concealed his theft); ﴿you argued﴾, i.e. you disputed ﴿on their behalf﴾, that is, on behalf of Ṭu'ma and his kin. It is also read ﴿on his behalf﴾. ﴿in the life of this world; but who will argue with God on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection﴾ when He punishes them? ﴿Or who will be a guardian over them﴾, one who takes charge of their affairs and defends them? That is, no one does so.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 4, verse 110:

﴿And whoever commits an evil﴾, a sin that harms another, like the throwing (of the blame) by Ṭu'ma al-Yahudi (the Jew), ﴿or wrongs himself﴾ by committing a sin limited to himself, ﴿then seeks forgiveness of Allah﴾ for it, i.e., repents, ﴿he will find Allah Forgiving﴾ to him, ﴿Merciful﴾ to him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 111:

﴿And whoever earns a sin﴾ (ithman), meaning a wrongdoing, ﴿then he earns it only against himself﴾, because its burden falls upon him, and it does not harm anyone else. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ in His doing.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 112:

﴿And whoever commits a sin﴾ a minor offence, ﴿or a misdeed﴾ a major offence, ﴿then throws it upon an innocent person﴾ of it, ﴿has certainly borne a slander﴾ he has taken upon himself, ﴿and a manifest sin﴾ clear, which he has committed by casting it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 113:

﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿and His mercy﴾ by preserving you (from error), ﴿a group of them would have resolved﴾ (ahmara, i.e., secretly intended) ﴿to mislead you﴾ from judging by the truth, by confusing you ﴿from among them﴾, from the people of Ṭu'mah, ﴿but they mislead none except themselves, and they cause you no harm in anything﴾, the word min (in min shay') being extra (zā'idah), ﴿for the consequence of their misleading falls upon themselves﴾. ﴿And Allah has sent down to you the Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and the wisdom﴾, meaning the rulings contained in it, ﴿and taught you what you did not know﴾, meaning the rulings and the unseen matters. ﴿And the grace of Allah upon you has been great﴾, by this and by other things.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 114:

﴿There is no good in much of their secret talk,﴾ i.e., of the people; that is, what they confer about and discuss, ﴿except﴾ the secret talk of ﴿one who enjoins charity, or what is right, or reconciliation between people.﴾ Right conduct. ﴿And whoever does that,﴾ the aforementioned, ﴿seeking﴾ seeking ﴿the good pleasure of Allah,﴾ not anything else of worldly affairs. ﴿Then We will give him,﴾ with the nun or the ya' (both readings), i.e., Allah, ﴿a great reward.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 115:

﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger﴾ contradicts him ﴿in what has come to him of guidance, after guidance has become clear to him﴾ the truth has become evident to him through the miracles, ﴿and follows other than the way of the believers﴾ i.e., their way, which is the religion they hold, by disbelieving ﴿We shall turn him to what he has turned to﴾ We shall make him responsible for what he has taken up of error, by leaving him to it in this world ﴿and burn him in Hell﴾ We shall cause him to enter it in the Hereafter, so that he burns therein ﴿and evil is it as a destination﴾ a return, it is.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 116:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with; but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly strayed far astray.﴾ far from the truth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 117:

﴿In﴾ (not) what they invoke ﴿yad'una﴾ (they worship), the idolaters, ﴿min dunihi﴾ (apart from Him), i.e., Allah, i.e., other than Him, ﴿illa inathan﴾ (except females), idols in the feminine form, like al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat. ﴿Wa in﴾ (and not) what they ﴿yad'una﴾ (worship, by worshipping them) ﴿illa shaytanan maridan﴾ (except a rebellious devil), one who has gone out of obedience, by their obedience to him in it, and he is Iblis.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 118:

﴿Allah cursed him﴾ — He removed him far from His mercy. ﴿And he said﴾ — i.e., Satan. ﴿"I will surely take﴾ — I will make for myself ﴿of Your servants a portion﴾ — a share ﴿obligatory﴾ — determined, cut off — I will call them to my obedience.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 4, verse 119:

﴿And I will surely mislead them﴾ from the truth through whispering; ﴿and I will surely arouse in them false desires﴾ — I will cast into their hearts long life and the denial of resurrection and reckoning; ﴿and I will surely command them so they will slit the ears of cattle﴾ — they will cut them off; and he did that with the baheerah (she-camel whose ears were slit as a mark of superstition); ﴿and I will surely command them so they will alter the creation of Allah﴾ — His religion, by disbelief, and by making lawful what Allah has forbidden and forbidding what Allah has made lawful; ﴿And whoever takes Satan as a guardian﴾ — who takes him as an ally and obeys him; ﴿instead of Allah﴾ — i.e., other than Him; ﴿he has certainly suffered a clear loss﴾ — evidently, because of his destination to the Fire, which is everlasting for him.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Tafsir of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 4, verse 120:

﴿He promises them﴾ long life, ﴿and arouses in them desires﴾ attaining their hopes in this world, and that there will be no resurrection and no recompense; ﴿but Satan promises them only delusion﴾ falsehood.
﴿Those: their refuge is Hell, and they will find no escape from it.﴾ [Mahaliyy] "a place of escape."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 122:

﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds – We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is true; and who is more truthful than Allah in statement?﴾ i.e., Allah promised them that, and His promise is true, truly. ﴿And who﴾ i.e., no one ﴿is more truthful than Allah in statement?﴾ i.e., in speech.

It was revealed when the Muslims and the People of the Book boasted. ﴿Not﴾ the matter is determined ﴿by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book﴾, but by righteous deeds. ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, either in the Hereafter or in this world through calamities and trials, as is related in the hadith. ﴿And he will not find for himself, besides Allah,﴾ i.e., other than Him, ﴿any protecting friend﴾ who will guard him, ﴿nor any helper﴾ who will prevent it from him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 124:

﴿And whoever does﴾ some of the righteous deeds, ﴿whether male or female, while he is a believer, those will enter﴾ with the verb in the passive voice and in the active voice (yadkhulūna / yudkhalūna), ﴿Paradise, and they will not be wronged﴾ even ﴿a speck﴾, the amount of the dent in a date-pit.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 125:

﴿And who⟩ meaning, no one ⟨is better in religion than one who submits his face⟩ meaning, submits himself and makes his deeds sincere ⟨to Allah, while he is a doer of good⟩ meaning, a monotheist ⟨and follows the creed of Ibrahim⟩ the one that agrees with the creed of Islam ⟨as a hanif⟩ a circumstantial state, meaning inclining away from all religions toward the upright religion ⟨and Allah took Ibrahim as a khalil⟩ a sincere friend, one of purest love for Him.

And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, [belonging to Him] in dominion, creation and servitude. ﴿And Allah is ever, of all things, encompassing﴾ in knowledge and power; that is, He has never ceased to be characterized by that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 127:

﴿They ask you for a ruling﴾ they request from you a ruling (fatwa) ﴿concerning﴾ the matter of ﴿women﴾ and their inheritance. ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and what is recited to you in the Book﴾ the Qur'an, from the verse of inheritance. And He also gives you a ruling ﴿concerning the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed﴾ ordained ﴿for them﴾ of inheritance, ﴿while you desire﴾ O guardians, ﴿to marry them﴾ out of disdain for their lack of beauty, and you prevent them from marrying others, hoping for their inheritance. That is, He rules that you must not do this. ﴿And [concerning] the oppressed﴾ young ones ﴿among the children﴾ that you should give them their rights. ﴿And that﴾ He commands you ﴿to stand firm for orphans in justice﴾ with fairness regarding inheritance and dower. ﴿And whatever good you do, indeed Allah is ever Knowing of it﴾ and He will reward you for it.

﴿And if a woman﴾ is in the nominative (*marfūʿ*, keep the Arabic *marfūʿ*), governed by an implied verb which the following word explains: ﴿fears﴾ (*khāfat*), meaning she anticipates ﴿from her husband﴾ (*baʿlihā*), that is, her husband (*zawjahā*), ﴿ill-treatment (nushūz)﴾, meaning arrogance toward her by abandoning her bed and falling short in her maintenance, out of dislike for her and the aspiration of his eye toward someone more beautiful than her. ﴿Or aversion﴾ (*iʿrāḍan*), meaning he turns away from her with his face. ﴿Then there is no blame upon them both if they make peace﴾ (*an yuṣliḥā*). In it, the *tāʾ* of the original form is assimilated (*idghām*, assimilation of one letter into the next) into the *ṣād*. In another recitation (*qirāʾah*, a mode of reading the Qurʾan), it is *yuṣliḥā* from *aṣlaḥa*. ﴿A settlement between them, a settlement﴾ concerning the division of nights and maintenance, by which she leaves some of her rights to him, seeking the continuation of the companionship. If she agrees to that, well and good; otherwise, the husband must give her her due right or part from her. ﴿And settlement is better﴾ than separation, ill-treatment and aversion. Almighty God said, explaining what humankind is created with: ﴿And souls are present with stinginess﴾, meaning extreme avarice. That is, they are created with it, as if it is present with them and never absent from them. The meaning is that a woman hardly ever gives up her share of her husband, and a man hardly ever gives up his self for her when he loves someone else. ﴿And if you do good﴾ in treating women well ﴿and fear God﴾ by avoiding injustice toward them, ﴿then indeed God is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾, and He will reward you for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 129:

﴿And you will never be able to be equitable between wives,﴾ i.e., make them equal ﴿in love,﴾ ﴿even if you should strive to do so.﴾ ﴿So do not incline completely [away from one wife]﴾ towards the one you love, in the division of nights and in maintenance, ﴿and leave her﴾ i.e., leave her hanging, ﴿as if in suspension﴾ — neither a woman without a husband (ayyim), nor one who has a husband. ﴿And if you amend﴾ through justice in the division ﴿and fear Allah﴾ against injustice, ﴿indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ of what is in your hearts of inclination ﴿and Merciful﴾ to you in that.

And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance (i.e., by His bounty), by providing the woman with another husband and providing him with another wife. And Allah is ever All-Encompassing (wāsiʿan) in bounty for His creation, All-Wise (ḥakīman) in what He ordains for them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 131:

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And We have certainly enjoined those who were given the Scripture before you, and [enjoined] you, [to], "Fear Allah."﴾ [The word] "scripture" [is used] in the sense of "scriptures." ﴿Before you﴾, i.e., the Jews and the Christians. ﴿And [We have enjoined] you﴾, O people of the Qur'an, ﴿[to]﴾, i.e., that, ﴿"Fear Allah"﴾, be wary of His punishment by obeying Him. ﴿And﴾ We said to them and to you, ﴿"If you disbelieve"﴾ in what you were enjoined, ﴿then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ in creation, dominion and servitude, so your disbelief does not harm Him. ﴿And Allah is ever Free of need﴾ of His creation and their worship, ﴿Praiseworthy﴾, praised in His actions toward them.

And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. [He] repeated it for emphasis, to establish the requirement of taqwa (God-consciousness). ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾, [meaning] as a witness that whatever is in them belongs to Him.
If He wills, He can take you away, O mankind, and bring others (in your place).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 4, verse 134:

﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world﴾ by his deed, ﴿with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter﴾ for whoever desires it, not with anyone else. So let none of you seek the lowest, and why not seek the highest by sincerity toward Him, since its object is found only with Him.

O you who have believed, be persistent in upholding justice (qiwam, standing firm), witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more entitled to both of them [than you are], and more knowing of their interests. So do not follow [your] desire (al-hawa) in your testimony, by favoring the rich for his pleasure or the poor out of pity for him, [so] that you not deviate (ta'dilu) from the truth. And if you distort (talwu) the testimony, or refuse (tu'ridu) to give it, then indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted, and He will reward you for it.

Note on the text: the translation above is a rendering of the passage as given, with the Qur'anic verse meanings in plain English. Two items are not fully reproduced here: the glosses of the words "qiwam" and "al-hawa" are supplied in parentheses in the English rendering to aid readability, and the Arabic "ta'dilu" and "talwu" are transliterated as they stand in the text. The passage also contains a qira'a (variant reading) note about omitting the first waw in talwu for lightening; that note has been left out of the translation above.

O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book He sent down upon His Messenger, [Muhammad (ﷺ)], and the Book He sent down before. (Those who believe, persist in belief.) [﴿يا أيّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا آمِنُوا﴾: "O you who have believed, believe" — the first is addressed to those who have believed, meaning: persist in faith.] ﴿بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ والكِتابِ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ عَلى رَسُولِهِ﴾ "in Allah and His Messenger and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger," i.e., Muhammad (ﷺ), and this is the Qur'an. ﴿والكِتابِ الَّذِي أنْزَلَ مِن قَبْلُ﴾ "and the Book which He sent down before," upon the messengers, with the meaning of "books" (kutub). In one recitation, the verbs in both places are read in the active voice (bi'l-bina' lil-fa'il). ﴿ومَن يَكْفُرْ بِاللَّهِ ومَلائِكَتِهِ وكُتُبِهِ ورُسُلِهِ واليَوْمِ الآخِرِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلالًا بَعِيدًا﴾ "And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, has certainly strayed far away," i.e., far from the truth.

Verse 137 of Surah 4 (an-Nisa'), with Jalalayn commentary:

﴿Indeed, those who believed﴾ in Musa, and they are the Jews, ﴿then disbelieved﴾ by worshipping the calf, ﴿then believed﴾ after him, ﴿then disbelieved﴾ in Isa, ﴿then increased in disbelief﴾ in Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿Allah would not have forgiven them﴾ so long as they persisted in it, ﴿nor would He guide them to a way﴾ a path to the truth.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on 4:138 (commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti):

﴿Bashshir﴾ (give good news; i.e., inform) O Muhammad, ﴿the hypocrites that for them there is a painful torment﴾ (painful, causing pain), which is the torment of the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 139:

﴿Those who⦆ is either a substitute (badal) or a qualifying adjective (na't) for "the hypocrites," ﴿who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers﴾ because of the strength they imagine in them. ﴿Do they seek⦆ i.e., they seek ﴿honour with them?﴾ This is an interrogative of denial, meaning: they do not find it with them. ﴿Indeed, honour belongs to God entirely﴾ in this world and the Hereafter, and none attains it except His allies.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 140:

﴿And He has already sent down to you in the Book﴾ (the Qur'an) in Surat al-An'am, ﴿that﴾ (an-, here the lightened form, mukhaffafah, whose noun is omitted, meaning that it is) ﴿when you hear the verses of Allah﴾ (the Qur'an) ﴿being disbelieved in and mocked, do not sit with them﴾ (i.e., the disbelievers and the mockers) ﴿until they engage in discourse other than that. Indeed, you would then be like them﴾ (if you sit with them) ﴿in sin﴾. ﴿Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hellfire all together﴾ as they were gathered in the world in disbelief and mockery.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 141:

﴿Alladhina﴾ is a substitute (badal) for the preceding ﴿alladhina﴾ ﴿yatarabbasuna﴾ wait (yantazirun) ﴿bikum﴾ for you, [to see] the reversals (al-dawa'ir) ﴿fa-in kana lakum fath﴾ if there is a victory and spoils for you ﴿min Allah﴾ from God, ﴿qalu﴾ they say [to you]: ﴿alam nakun ma'akum﴾ "Were we not with you" in the religion and the struggle (jihad), so give us a share of the spoils? ﴿wa-in kana lil-kafirina nasib﴾ and if the disbelievers have a share [of victory] over you, ﴿qalu﴾ they say [to them]: ﴿alam nastahwidh﴾ "Did we not gain mastery (nastawli) ﴿alaykum﴾ over you, and become able (naqdir) to seize you and kill you, but we spared you?" ﴿wa﴾ "Did we not" ﴿namna'kum min al-mu'minin﴾ protect you from the believers, [preventing them] from defeating you, by discouraging them (takhdhil) and by informing you of their news (bi-akhbarihim)? So we have a favour upon you. ﴿Fa-Allahu yahkumu baynakum﴾ God will judge between you and them ﴿yawm al-qiyama﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, by causing [you] to enter [the Fire] and causing them to enter the Fire. ﴿Wa-lan yaj'ala Allahu lil-kafirina 'ala al-mu'minina sabilan﴾ and God will never grant the disbelievers any way (tariq) over the believers by total annihilation (al-isti'sal).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 142:

﴿Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah﴾ by displaying the opposite of what they conceal of disbelief, so that they may ward off from themselves its worldly rulings. ﴿And He is their Deceiver﴾, meaning He will requite them for their deception, so they are disgraced in this world by Allah informing His Prophet of what they concealed, and they are punished in the Hereafter. ﴿And when they stand up to prayer﴾ with the believers, ﴿they stand up lazily﴾, reluctant and sluggish, ﴿showing off to the people﴾ through their prayer, ﴿and they do not remember Allah﴾, i.e., they do not pray, ﴿except a little﴾, out of show-off.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 143:

﴿Wavering⁠﴾ between that, wavering (mutaraddidin) between disbelief and belief, ﴿neither⁠﴾ belonging ﴿to these⁠﴾, i.e., the disbelievers, ﴿nor to those⁠﴾, i.e., the believers. ﴿And whomever Allah sends astray⁠﴾, and whomever Allah sends astray, ﴿you will not find for him a way⁠﴾, a path to guidance.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 144:

﴿O you who have believed, do not take disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do you wish to give Allah a clear authority against yourselves?﴾ By your allegiance to them, ﴿a clear authority﴾, meaning a manifest proof against your hypocrisy.

Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest level (al-dark, the place) of the Fire (al-asfal min al-nar), which is its deepest bottom (qa'ruha), "and you will not find for them any helper" (nasiran), one who will prevent them from the punishment.

Except those who repent [from hypocrisy] and make amends and hold fast to Allah and devote their religion sincerely to Allah [free from showing off]. Those will be with the believers, and Allah will give the believers a great reward [in the Hereafter, which is Paradise].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 147:

﴿What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful﴾ for His blessings ﴿and believe﴾ in Him? The interrogative here carries the sense of negation, meaning: He does not punish you. ﴿And Allah is ever Appreciative﴾ of the deeds of the believers, by rewarding them, ﴿Knowing﴾ of His creation.

God does not love the public utterance of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged (أي: يعاقبه عليه، أي لا يحب الله الجهر بالسوء من القول من أحد، أي يعاقبه عليه). Except by one who has been wronged, for He does not hold him to account for speaking of it openly, by informing about the wrong of his wrongdoer and invoking [God's curse] upon him. And God is ever All-Hearing of what is said, All-Knowing of what is done.

Note on the translation: the bracketed gloss in the source ("أي يعاقبه عليه") is reflected above in parentheses, and the Qur'anic text is rendered as follows:

﴿God does not love the public utterance of evil speech from anyone, meaning He will punish him for it, except one who has been wronged, for He does not hold him to account for speaking of it openly by informing about the wrong of his wrongdoer and invoking [God's curse] upon him. And God is ever All-Hearing of what is said, All-Knowing of what is done.﴾

"If you show what is good" (﴿إنْ تُبْدُوا﴾) means you display it (تُظْهِرُوا), "[any] good" (﴿خَيْرًا﴾) from acts of righteousness, "or conceal it" (﴿أوْ تُخْفُوهُ﴾) means you do it secretly (تَعْمَلُوهُ سِرًّا), "or pardon an evil" (﴿أوْ تَعْفُوا عَنْ سُوء﴾) meaning an injustice (ظُلْم).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 150:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and want to make distinction between Allah and His messengers﴾ by believing in Him without them, ﴿and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others"﴾ of the messengers, ﴿and want to adopt a path between that﴾ — between disbelief and belief — ﴿a way﴾, a road they take toward it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 151:

﴿Those are the disbelievers in truth.﴾ "Haqqan" (truly, in truth) is a verbal noun (maṣdar) emphasizing the content of the sentence before it. ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.﴾ "Muhīnan" (humiliating), i.e., bringing humiliation; it is the punishment of the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 152:

﴿Those who believe in Allah and His messengers﴾, all of them, ﴿and do not make distinction between any of them, those — He will give them their rewards﴾ — with the ya' and the nun (i.e., read as yu'tihim, "He will give them," or nu'tihim, "We will give them") — ﴿their rewards﴾, meaning the reward of their deeds. ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ toward His allies, ﴿Merciful﴾ toward the people of His obedience.

﴿They ask you﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿the People of the Book﴾, the Jews, ﴿to bring down to them a Book from heaven﴾, all at once, ﴿as was sent down to Moses﴾, out of ta'annut (obstinate, contentious defiance). ﴿If you consider that great,﴾ then ﴿they asked﴾, meaning their forefathers, ﴿Moses for something greater than that. They said: "Show us God openly"﴾, plainly, face to face. ﴿So the thunderbolt seized them﴾, meaning death, as a punishment for them ﴿for their wrongdoing﴾, since they were contentious in their question. ﴿Then they took the calf﴾ as a god ﴿after the clear proofs had come to them﴾, meaning the miracles attesting to God's oneness. ﴿And We pardoned that﴾ and did not wipe them out. ﴿And We gave Moses clear authority﴾, meaning manifest dominion over them, when he commanded them to kill themselves in repentance, and they obeyed him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 154:

﴿And We raised over them the mount (al-Tur)﴾ the mountain, ﴿for their covenant﴾ because of taking the covenant from them, so that they would fear, and they accepted it. ﴿And We said to them﴾ while it was overshadowing them, ﴿Enter the gate﴾ the gate of the town, ﴿prostrating﴾ prostration of bowing. ﴿And We said to them: Do not transgress﴾ and in another recitation it is read with a fatha on the ʿayn and a shadda on the dal, and in it the ta' of the original is assimilated into the dal, meaning: do not exceed bounds, ﴿in the Sabbath﴾ by hunting the fish in it. ﴿And We took from them a solemn covenant﴾ upon that, ﴿but they broke it﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 155:

﴿So for their breaking their covenant﴾ "mā" is extra (ziyāda), and the "bā'" is for causality (sababiyya), connected to an omitted verb, meaning: We cursed them because of their breaking ﴿their covenant, and their disbelief in the signs of Allah, and their killing of the prophets without right, and their saying﴾ to the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿"Our hearts are uncovered"﴾ (ghulf), not understanding your speech. ﴿Nay, Allah has sealed﴾ (ṭaba'a), meaning closed up, ﴿over them because of their disbelief﴾, so they do not understand admonition. ﴿So they do not believe, except a few﴾ of them, such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his companions.

﴿And for their disbelief﴾ secondly, in ʿĪsā (Jesus), and he repeated the preposition بِ (bi) to separate it from what it is conjoined with, ﴿and their saying against Maryam a tremendous slander﴾, where they accused her of fornication.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 157:

﴿And their saying﴾ boastfully, ﴿"Indeed, we killed the Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah"﴾ — according to their claim, meaning: for all of that We punished them. He, the Exalted, said, denying their claim that they killed him: ﴿And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear to them⁠﻿ like that﴾ — the one killed and crucified, who was their companion, appeared to them as Jesus; that is, Allah cast his likeness upon him, so they thought he was him. ﴿Indeed, those who differ concerning him﴾ — that is, concerning Jesus — ﴿are in doubt about it﴾, about his killing, since some of them said, when they saw the one killed, that his face was the face of Jesus but his body was not his body, so he was not him; and others said, "Rather, he is him." ﴿They have no knowledge of it﴾ — of his killing — ﴿except the following of assumption﴾. This is a disconnected exception, meaning: rather, they follow in it the assumption that they imagined. ﴿And they did not kill him with certainty﴾ — a confirming circumstantial clause emphasizing the negation of the killing.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 158:

﴿Rather, Allah raised him up to Himself, and Allah is ever Mighty⟩ in His dominion ﴿Wise⟩ in His creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 159:

﴿And there is not﴾ anyone ﴿of the People of the Scripture (ahl al-kitab)﴾ ﴿but will surely believe in him﴾, in Jesus, ﴿before his death﴾. That is, the People of the Scripture (kitabi) at the moment he witnesses the angels of death, when his faith will not benefit him. Or, before the death of Jesus, when he descends near the Hour, as is reported in a hadith. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection he will be﴾ Jesus ﴿a witness against them﴾ for what they did, when he was sent to them.

﴿Because of wrongdoing﴾, i.e., because of a wrong ﴿committed by those who were Jews﴾, namely the Jews. ﴿We forbade them good things that had been made lawful for them﴾. These are the things mentioned in His words, exalted is He: ﴿We forbade every animal with claws﴾, and the verse [continues]. ﴿And for their hindering﴾ people ﴿from the way of Allah﴾, His religion, ﴿hindering⁠﴾.

﴿And their taking of usury (ribā), although they had been forbidden from it﴾ in the Tawrah (Torah), ﴿and their consuming of people's wealth wrongfully﴾ by means of bribery in judgment, ﴿and We have prepared for those of them who disbelieve a painful punishment﴾, painful, causing pain.

Translation of the passage from Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 4, verse 162:

﴿But those firm in knowledge among them﴾ (al-rasikhun, i.e. those firmly established) ﴿the firmly established in knowledge among them, such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam﴾ ... 

Let me correct that: the translation proper follows.

﴿But those firmly grounded in knowledge among them﴾ (al-thabitun) ﴿such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam﴾ ﴿and the believers﴾ (al-mu'minun), ﴿the emigrants and the Helpers﴾ (al-Muhajirun wa-al-Ansar), ﴿believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you﴾ (min al-kutub), ﴿and those who establish the prayer﴾ (al-muqimin al-salah). It is put in the accusative (nusiba) by way of praise (ʿala al-madh), and it has also been read in the nominative (bi-al-raf'). ﴿And those who give zakat, and who believe in God and the Last Day﴾ (al-mu'tuna al-zakah wa-al-mu'minuna bi-Allah wa-al-yawm al-akhir), ﴿those — We shall give them﴾ (ulaʾika sa-nu'tihim), with the nun and with the ya' (bi-al-nun wa-al-ya'), ﴿a great reward﴾ (ajran ʿazimana), which is Paradise.

﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, and﴾ as ﴿We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac﴾ his two sons, ﴿and Jacob﴾ the son of Isaac, ﴿and the Tribes﴾ his descendants, ﴿and Solomon. And We gave﴾ to his father ﴿David the Psalms﴾. The word زَبُورًا (zabūran) with a fatḥa (the vowel "a") is the name of the book that was given, while with a ḍamma (the vowel "u") it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of مَزْبُورًا (mazbūran), meaning "written," i.e., مَكْتُوبًا (maktūban), "written down."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 164:

﴿And﴾ [We sent] ﴿messengers about whom We have already related to you before, and messengers about whom We have not related to you﴾. It is related that He, Exalted is He, sent eight thousand prophets: four thousand from the Children of Israel and four thousand from the rest of mankind. The Shaykh said this in Surat Ghafir. ﴿And Allah spoke to Moses﴾ directly, without an intermediary.

Messengers as good news-bearers (بَدَل from "رُسُلًا" before it), ﴿mubashshirin﴾ bringing good news of reward to whoever believes, and ﴿wa-mundhirin﴾ warning of punishment to whoever disbelieves. We sent them ﴿so that there would be no argument for people against God after the messengers﴾ (تُقال: i.e., "after" the sending of the messengers to them), so that they could not say: "Our Lord, if only You had sent us a messenger, we would have followed Your signs and been among the believers." So We sent them to cut off their excuse. ﴿And God is ever Mighty﴾ in His dominion, ﴿Wise﴾ in His creation.

It was revealed when the Jews were asked about his prophethood (ﷺ), and they denied it: ﴿But Allah bears witness﴾ to Your prophethood ﴿to what He has sent down to you﴾ of the Qur'an, which is miraculous, ﴿He has sent it down with His knowledge﴾ meaning, knowing it, or His knowledge is in it, ﴿and the angels bear witness﴾ to you too, ﴿and Allah suffices as a witness﴾ to that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 167:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾ in Allah ﴿and avert [others] from the way of Allah﴾, the religion of Islam, ﴿by concealing the description of Muhammad﴾ (ﷺ), ﴿and they are the Jews, ﴿have certainly strayed far astray﴾ from the truth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 168:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved﴾ in Allah ﴿and wronged﴾ His Prophet by concealing his description ﴿Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to any path﴾ of the paths.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 169:

﴿Except the path of Hell﴾, i.e., the path leading to it, ﴿abiding therein forever﴾, [those] destined to abide [in it] when they enter it, ﴿forever. And that is ever easy for Allah﴾, [meaning] effortless.

O mankind, meaning the people of Makkah. The Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ), has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe in him and aim for what is better for you than what you are in. But if you disbelieve, then to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, in dominion, creation and servitude; so your disbelief does not harm Him. Allah is All-Knowing of His creatures, All-Wise in His dealings with them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 4, verse 171:

﴿O People of the Book﴾, meaning the Gospel (al-Injil), ﴿do not go to excess in your religion, and do not say about God except the truth﴾, meaning, by declaring Him exalted (tanzih) above partners and offspring. ﴿The Messiah, Jesus, son of Mary, was only a messenger of God and His word which He conveyed﴾, meaning He delivered it, ﴿to Mary, and a spirit﴾, meaning one possessing a soul (dhu ruh), ﴿from Him﴾. It is ascribed to Him, exalted is He, as an honour to him. ﴿And [it is] not [as] you claim: "a son of God," or "a god with Him," or "a third of three," because the one possessing a soul is composed, whereas God is exalted above composition and above attributing a composite thing to Him.﴾ ﴿So believe in God and His messengers, and do not say "Three." Desist, [it is] better for you.﴾ That is, desist from this and do what is better for you, namely the affirmation of God's oneness (tawhid). ﴿God is only one God; glory be to Him﴾, exalting Him above ﴿having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, by creation, dominion and ownership. Being owned (al-malakiyya) contradicts being a son (prophethood). ﴿And sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs﴾, meaning as a witness to that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 172:

﴿Never would the Messiah disdain﴾ to be proud and reject, ﴿the Messiah﴾, whom you claimed to be a god, ﴿from being a servant of Allah, nor would the angels, the near ones﴾ with Allah, ﴿disdain﴾ to be servants. This is from the finest digression (istitrad), mentioned to refute those who claimed that they are gods or daughters of Allah, just as the preceding verse refuted the Christians who made that claim; the intended addressees being them. ﴿And whoever disdains His worship and is proud, He will gather them all to Himself﴾ in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 173:

﴿So as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards﴾ the reward of their deeds, ﴿and increase them from His bounty﴾ what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no thought has occurred to a human heart. ﴿And as for those who disdained and were arrogant﴾ toward His worship, ﴿He will punish them with a painful punishment﴾ painful, which is the punishment of the Fire. ﴿And they will not find for themselves, other than Allah,﴾ i.e., besides Him, ﴿any protector﴾ who would repel it from them, ﴿or any helper﴾ who would prevent them from it.

O mankind, there has come to you a proof (ḥujjah) from your Lord, [meaning against you], and it is the Prophet (ﷺ). And We have sent down to you a clear light, [meaning manifest], and it is the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 175:

﴿As for those who believed in Allah and held fast to Him, He will admit them into mercy from Him and bounty, and guide them to Himself on a path [that is] straight﴾ — a way, [that is] straight — it is the religion of Islam.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 4, verse 176:

﴿They ask you for a legal pronouncement﴾ concerning al-kalala (the one who dies leaving neither ascendants nor descendants). ﴿Say: Allah gives you a pronouncement concerning al-kalala. If a man dies﴾ is in the nominative, governed by a verb implied by the following word, which explains it: ﴿dies﴾ (māta), ﴿leaving no child﴾, i.e., no child nor parent, and this is al-kalala, ﴿and he has a sister﴾ from both parents or from the father. ﴿Then she has half of what he leaves, and he﴾ (i.e., the brother) likewise ﴿inherits from her all of what she leaves﴾ ﴿if she has no child.﴾ If she has a male child, he gets nothing; if a female child, he gets what remains of her share. And even if the sister or brother is from the mother's side, their share is a sixth, as mentioned at the beginning of the surah. ﴿If there are two﴾ (i.e., the two sisters), that is, two or more, because it was revealed concerning Jabir, who died leaving sisters, ﴿then they have two-thirds of what he left.﴾ ﴿And if they are siblings, men and women, then the male has the equivalent of the share of two females.﴾ ﴿Allah makes clear to you﴾ the laws of your religion ﴿so that﴾ you do not ﴿go astray. And Allah has knowledge of all things﴾, and among them is inheritance. Al-Shaykhan narrated from al-Bara' that it was the last verse revealed, i.e., of the obligatory shares (al-fara'id, the prescribed inheritance portions).
